title.raw: 卷三十九 志第二十九 百官上 Volume 39 Treatises 29: Officials 1

sentences.zh: 太宰，一人。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor (Taizai), one post.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor: one office.

sentences.zh: 周武王時，周公旦始居之，掌邦治，為六卿之首。

translations.literal: In the time of King Wu of Zhou, the Duke of Zhou Dan first held this office, governing the state, and was head of the Six Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of King Wu of Zhou, the Duke of Zhou, Dan, was the first to hold the post; he governed the realm and stood at the head of the Six Ministers.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢、魏不常置。

translations.literal: Under Qin, Han, and Wei it was not regularly established.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qin, Han, and Wei dynasties the office was not kept in regular use.

sentences.zh: 晉初依周禮，備置三公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin, following the Rites of Zhou, the Three Dukes were fully established.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Jin, the court followed the Rites of Zhou and restored the full complement of the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 三公之職，太師居首，景帝名師，故置太宰以代之。

translations.literal: Among the duties of the Three Dukes, the Grand Preceptor (Taishi) ranked first; because Emperor Jing's given name was Shi, the Grand Preceptor (Taizai) was established to replace it.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Three Dukes, the Grand Preceptor (Taishi) had ranked first; because Emperor Jing's personal name contained shi, the court established the Grand Preceptor (Taizai) in its place.

sentences.zh: 太宰，蓋古之太師也。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor (Taizai) was essentially the ancient Grand Preceptor (Taishi).
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor (Taizai) was in effect the ancient office of Grand Preceptor (Taishi).

sentences.zh: 殷紂之時，箕子為太師。

translations.literal: In the time of King Zhou of Yin, Jizi served as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Under King Zhou of Yin, Jizi held the post of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 周武王時，太公為太師。

translations.literal: In the time of King Wu of Zhou, the Grand Duke served as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of King Wu of Zhou, the Grand Duke (Jiang Ziya) served as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 周成王時，周公為太師。

translations.literal: In the time of King Cheng of Zhou, the Duke of Zhou served as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Under King Cheng of Zhou, the Duke of Zhou served as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 周公薨，畢公代之。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Zhou died, the Duke of Bi succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Duke of Zhou's death, the Duke of Bi took his place.

sentences.zh: 漢西京初不置，平帝始復置太師官，而孔光居焉。

translations.literal: Early Western Han did not establish it; Emperor Ping first restored the Grand Preceptor office, and Kong Guang held it.
translations.idiomatic: Early Western Han did not maintain the office; Emperor Ping was the first to restore the post of Grand Preceptor, which Kong Guang then held.

sentences.zh: 漢東京又廢。

translations.literal: Eastern Han abolished it again.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han abolished the office once more.

sentences.zh: 獻帝初，董卓為太師，卓誅又廢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xian's reign, Dong Zhuo served as Grand Preceptor; after Zhuo was executed it was abolished again.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xian's reign Dong Zhuo held the post of Grand Preceptor; after Zhuo was killed the office was abolished again.

sentences.zh: 魏世不置。

translations.literal: Wei did not establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei the office was not established.

sentences.zh: 晉既因太師而置太宰，以安平王孚居焉。

translations.literal: Jin, having established Grand Preceptor (Taizai) in place of Grand Preceptor (Taishi), had the Prince of Ping'an, Sima Fu, hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then created the Grand Preceptor (Taizai) to replace the Grand Preceptor (Taishi), and the Prince of Ping'an, Sima Fu, held the office.

sentences.zh: 太傅，一人。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor (Taifu), one post.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor: one office.

sentences.zh: 周成王時，畢公為太傅。

translations.literal: In the time of King Cheng of Zhou, the Duke of Bi served as Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Under King Cheng of Zhou, the Duke of Bi served as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 漢高后元年，初用王陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Empress Gao of Han, Wang Ling was first appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Empress Gao's regency, Wang Ling became the first appointee.

sentences.zh: 太保，一人。

translations.literal: Grand Guardian (Taibao), one post.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Guardian: one office.

sentences.zh: 殷太甲時，伊尹為太保。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Taijia of Yin, Yi Yin served as Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taijia of Yin, Yi Yin served as Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 周武王時，召公為太保。

translations.literal: In the time of King Wu of Zhou, the Duke of Shao served as Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of King Wu of Zhou, the Duke of Shao served as Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 漢平帝元始元年，始用王舜。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanshi of Emperor Ping of Han, Wang Shun was first appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanshi under Emperor Ping of Han, Wang Shun was the first appointee.

sentences.zh: 後漢至魏不置，晉初復置焉。

translations.literal: Later Han through Wei did not establish it; at the beginning of Jin it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: From Later Han through Wei the office was not kept; it was restored at the founding of Jin.

sentences.zh: 自太師至太保，是為三公。

translations.literal: From Grand Preceptor (Taishi) to Grand Guardian, these are the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: From the Grand Preceptor through the Grand Guardian—these are the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 論道經邦，燮理陰陽，無其人則闕，所以訓護人主，導以德義者。

translations.literal: They discuss the Way and govern the state, harmonize yin and yang; when there is no suitable person the posts remain vacant—they exist to instruct and protect the ruler, guiding him through virtue and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: They discourse on the Way and steward the realm, harmonizing yin and yang; when no worthy man is at hand the posts are left unfilled. Their purpose is to instruct and safeguard the sovereign, guiding him by virtue and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 相國，一人。

translations.literal: Chancellor of State (Xiangguo), one post.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor of State: one office.

sentences.zh: 漢高帝十一年始置，以蕭何居之，罷丞相；

translations.literal: Established in the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu of Han, with Xiao He holding it; the office of Chancellor was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: It was first established in the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu of Han, with Xiao He in the post; the Chancellor's office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 何薨，曹參代之；

translations.literal: When He died, Cao Shen succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao He died, Cao Shen succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 參薨，罷。

translations.literal: When Shen died, the office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shen died, the office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 魏齊王以晉景帝為相國。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Qi of Qi in Wei, Emperor Jing of Jin was made Chancellor of State.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi ruler of Wei, the future Emperor Jing of Jin was appointed Chancellor of State.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝時趙王倫，愍帝時南陽王保，安帝時宋高祖，順帝時齊王，並為相國。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Hui of Jin, Prince Lun of Zhao; under Emperor Min, Prince Bao of Nanyang; under Emperor An, the Song founder; under Emperor Shun, the Prince of Qi—all served as Chancellor of State.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui of Jin, Prince Lun of Zhao; under Emperor Min, Prince Bao of Nanyang; under Emperor An, the founder of Song; under Emperor Shun, the Prince of Qi—all held the title of Chancellor of State.

sentences.zh: 自魏、晉以來，非復人臣之位矣。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, it was no longer a position for mere subjects.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward it was no longer a post fit for an ordinary subject.

sentences.zh: 丞相，一人。

translations.literal: Chancellor (Chengxiang), one post.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor: one office.

sentences.zh: 殷湯以伊尹為右相，仲虺為左相。

translations.literal: King Tang of Yin appointed Yi Yin as Right Chancellor and Zhong Hui as Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: King Tang of Yin made Yi Yin Right Chancellor and Zhong Hui Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 秦悼武王二年，始置丞相官。

translations.literal: In the second year of King Daowu of Qin, the office of Chancellor was first established.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of King Daowu of Qin the office of Chancellor was first created.

sentences.zh: 丞，奉。

translations.literal: Cheng means "to receive" or "to support."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng means "to receive" or "to uphold."

sentences.zh: 相，助也。

translations.literal: Xiang means "to assist."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang means "to assist."

sentences.zh: 悼武王子昭襄王始以樗里疾為丞相，後又置左右丞相。

translations.literal: King Zhaoxiang of Qin, son of King Daowu, first appointed Chuli Ji as Chancellor; later he also established Left and Right Chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhaoxiang, son of King Daowu, first appointed Chuli Ji as Chancellor; later he also created the offices of Left and Right Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 漢高帝初，置一丞相，十一年，更名相國。

translations.literal: In early Han under Gaozu, one Chancellor was established; in the eleventh year it was renamed Chancellor of State.
translations.idiomatic: Early under Emperor Gaozu of Han a single Chancellor was appointed; in the eleventh year the title was changed to Chancellor of State.

sentences.zh: 孝惠、高后置左右丞相，文帝二年，復置一丞相。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Gao, Left and Right Chancellors were established; in the second year of Emperor Wen, one Chancellor was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Gao, Left and Right Chancellors were appointed; in the second year of Emperor Wen a single Chancellor was restored.

sentences.zh: 哀帝元壽二年，更名大司徒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanshou of Emperor Ai, it was renamed Grand Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanshou under Emperor Ai the office was renamed Grand Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 漢東京不復置。

translations.literal: Eastern Han did not restore it.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han did not restore the office.

sentences.zh: 至獻帝建安十三年，復置丞相，魏世及晉初又廢。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an of Emperor Xian, Chancellor was restored; Wei and early Jin abolished it again.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an under Emperor Xian the Chancellor was restored; under Wei and early Jin it was abolished once more.

sentences.zh: 惠帝世，趙王倫篡位，以梁王肜為丞相。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Hui, when Prince Lun of Zhao usurped the throne, the Prince of Liang Yin was made Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Hui, when Prince Lun of Zhao seized the throne, Prince Yin of Liang was appointed Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 永興元年，以成都王穎為丞相。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxing, the Prince of Chengdu Ying was made Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongxing, Prince Ying of Chengdu was made Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 愍帝建興元年，以琅邪王睿為左丞相，南陽王保為右丞相；

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianxing of Emperor Min, Prince Rui of Langye was Left Chancellor and Prince Bao of Nanyang was Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianxing under Emperor Min, Prince Rui of Langye was Left Chancellor and Prince Bao of Nanyang was Right Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 三年，以保為相國，睿為丞相。

translations.literal: In the third year, Bao was made Chancellor of State and Rui was Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Bao was made Chancellor of State and Rui was made Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 元帝永昌元年，以王敦為丞相，轉司徒荀組為太尉，以司徒官屬并丞相為留府，敦不受。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang of Emperor Yuan, Wang Dun was made Chancellor; Minister over the Masses Xun Zu was transferred to Grand Commandant, and the staff of the Minister over the Masses office was merged into the Chancellor's office left at the capital; Dun refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchang under Emperor Yuan, Wang Dun was made Chancellor; Xun Zu was moved from Minister over the Masses to Grand Commandant, and the Minister over the Masses staff was merged into the Chancellor's office left at the capital—but Dun refused.

sentences.zh: 成帝世，以王導為丞相，罷司徒府以為丞相府，導薨，罷丞相，復為司徒府。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Cheng, Wang Dao was Chancellor; the Minister over the Masses office was abolished to become the Chancellor's office; when Dao died, Chancellor was abolished and the Minister over the Masses office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng, Wang Dao was Chancellor; the Minister over the Masses office was dissolved to serve as the Chancellor's office. When Dao died, the Chancellorship was abolished and the Minister over the Masses office was restored.

sentences.zh: 宋世祖初，以南郡王義宣為丞相，而司徒府如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizu of Song, Prince Xuan of Nanjun was Chancellor, while the Minister over the Masses office remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Shizu's reign in Song, Prince Xuan of Nanjun was Chancellor, while the Minister over the Masses office remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 太尉，一人。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant (Taiwei), one post.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant: one office.

sentences.zh: 自上安下曰尉。

translations.literal: Wei means one who secures peace from above to below.
translations.idiomatic: Wei denotes one who brings security from above down to the people below.

sentences.zh: 掌兵事，郊祀掌亞獻，大喪則告諡南郊。

translations.literal: In charge of military affairs; at suburban sacrifices assists in the second offering; at a great mourning announces the posthumous title at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw military affairs; at suburban sacrifices he performed the secondary offering; at a state funeral he announced the posthumous title at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 堯時舜為太尉官，漢因之。

translations.literal: In the time of Yao, Shun held the office of Grand Commandant; Han followed this.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Yao, Shun held the office of Grand Commandant; Han adopted the precedent.

sentences.zh: 武帝建元二年省。

translations.literal: Abolished in the second year of Jianyuan of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished in the second year of Jianyuan under Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 光武建武二十七年，罷大司馬，置太尉以代之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu of Guangwu, Grand Commander-in-Chief was abolished and Grand Commandant replaced it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu, Emperor Guangwu abolished the Grand Commander-in-Chief and established the Grand Commandant in its place.

sentences.zh: 靈帝末，以劉虞為大司馬，而太尉如故。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Ling, Liu Yu was made Grand Commander-in-Chief, while Grand Commandant remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Ling's reign Liu Yu was made Grand Commander-in-Chief, while the Grand Commandant continued as before.

sentences.zh: 司徒，一人。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses (Situ), one post.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses: one office.

sentences.zh: 掌民事，郊祀掌省牲視濯，大喪安梓宮。

translations.literal: In charge of civil affairs; at suburban sacrifices inspects the sacrificial animals and washes them; at a great mourning settles the spirit coffin.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw civil affairs; at suburban sacrifices he inspected the victims and supervised their washing; at a state funeral he settled the spirit coffin in place.

sentences.zh: 少昊氏以鳥名官，而祝鳩氏為司徒。

translations.literal: Shaohao named offices after birds, and the Zhujiushou clan served as Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Shaohao named offices after birds, and the Zhujiushou clan held the post of Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 堯時舜為司徒。

translations.literal: In the time of Yao, Shun was Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Yao, Shun served as Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 舜攝帝位，命契為司徒。

translations.literal: When Shun assumed the imperial position, he appointed Qi as Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun took charge of the imperial duties, he appointed Qi Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 契玄孫之孫曰微，亦為夏司徒。

translations.literal: Qi's great-grandson's grandson was called Wei, who also served as Minister over the Masses under Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's great-grandson's grandson, named Wei, also served as Minister over the Masses under the Xia.

sentences.zh: 周時司徒為地官，掌邦教。

translations.literal: In Zhou the Minister over the Masses was the Minister of Earth, in charge of state education.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou the Minister over the Masses was the Minister of Earth, charged with the state's instruction.

sentences.zh: 漢西京初不置。

translations.literal: Early Western Han did not establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Early Western Han did not maintain the office.

sentences.zh: 哀帝元壽二年，罷丞相，罷大司徒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanshou of Emperor Ai, the Chancellor was abolished, and the Grand Minister over the Masses was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanshou under Emperor Ai the Chancellor was abolished and the Grand Minister over the Masses was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 光武建武二十七年，去大。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu of Guangwu, the character "Grand" was removed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu, Emperor Guangwu dropped the word "Grand" from the title.

sentences.zh: 司空，一人。

translations.literal: Minister of Works (Sikong), one post.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works (Sikong): one office.

sentences.zh: 掌水土事，郊祀掌掃除陳樂器，大喪掌將校復土。

translations.literal: In charge of water and earth affairs; at suburban sacrifices sweeps, arranges musical instruments; at a great mourning directs officers in returning earth.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw water and earthworks; at suburban sacrifices he swept the ground and set out the musical instruments; at a state funeral he directed officers in the burial rites of returning earth.

sentences.zh: 舜攝帝位，以禹為司空。

translations.literal: When Shun assumed the imperial position, he appointed Yu as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun took charge of the imperial duties, he made Yu Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 契玄孫之子曰冥，亦為夏司空。

translations.literal: Qi's great-grandson's son was called Ming, who also served as Minister of Works under Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's great-grandson's son, named Ming, also served as Minister of Works under the Xia.

sentences.zh: 殷湯以咎單為司空。

translations.literal: King Tang of Yin appointed Gao Dan as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: King Tang of Yin appointed Gao Dan Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 周時司空為冬官，掌邦事。

translations.literal: In Zhou the Minister of Works was the Minister of Winter, in charge of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou the Minister of Works was the Minister of Winter, charged with the state's affairs.

sentences.zh: 漢西京初不置。

translations.literal: Early Western Han did not establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Early Western Han did not maintain the office.

sentences.zh: 成帝綏和元年，更名御史大夫為大司空；

translations.literal: In the first year of Weihe of Emperor Cheng, the Censor-in-Chief was renamed Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Weihe under Emperor Cheng the Censor-in-Chief was renamed Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 哀帝建平二年，復為御史大夫；

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianping of Emperor Ai, it was restored as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianping under Emperor Ai it was changed back to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 元壽二年，復為大司空；

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanshou, it was again Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanshou it was again Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 光武建武二十七年去大字。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu of Guangwu the character "Grand" was removed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu, Emperor Guangwu dropped the word "Grand."

sentences.zh: 獻帝建安十三年，又罷司空，置御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an of Emperor Xian, Minister of Works was again abolished and Censor-in-Chief established.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an under Emperor Xian the Minister of Works was abolished again and the Censor-in-Chief was established.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫郗慮免，不復補。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xi Lü was dismissed and not replaced.
translations.idiomatic: The Censor-in-Chief Xi Lü was dismissed and the post was never filled again.

sentences.zh: 魏初又置司空。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wei, Minister of Works was again established.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Wei the Minister of Works was restored.

sentences.zh: 大司馬，一人。

translations.literal: Grand Commander-in-Chief (Dasima), one post.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commander-in-Chief: one office.

sentences.zh: 掌武事。

translations.literal: In charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw military affairs.

sentences.zh: 司，主也。

translations.literal: Si means "to direct" or "to preside."
translations.idiomatic: Si means "to direct" or "to preside over."

sentences.zh: 馬，武也。

translations.literal: Ma means "military."
translations.idiomatic: Ma denotes the military.

sentences.zh: 堯時棄為后稷，兼掌司馬。

translations.literal: In the time of Yao, Qi served as Director of Agriculture and also oversaw military affairs as Sima.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Yao, Qi served as Director of Agriculture and also held charge of military affairs as Sima.

sentences.zh: 周時司馬為夏官，掌邦政。

translations.literal: In Zhou the Sima was the Minister of Summer, in charge of state government.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou the Sima was the Minister of Summer, charged with the state's administration.

sentences.zh: 項籍以曹無咎、周殷並為大司馬。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu appointed Cao Wujiu and Zhou Yin both as Grand Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu appointed Cao Wujiu and Zhou Yin both Grand Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 漢初不置。

translations.literal: Early Han did not establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han did not maintain the office.

sentences.zh: 武帝元狩四年，初置大司馬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanshou of Emperor Wu, Grand Commander-in-Chief was first established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu the Grand Commander-in-Chief was first created.

sentences.zh: 始直云司馬，議者以漢有軍候千人司馬官，故加大。

translations.literal: At first it was simply called Sima; deliberators held that Han already had a Sima office among the thousand-household military attendants, so "Grand" was added.
translations.idiomatic: At first the title was simply Sima; critics noted that Han already had a Sima post among the thousand-household military attendants, so the prefix "Grand" was added.

sentences.zh: 及置司空，又以縣道官有獄司空，又加大。

translations.literal: When Sikong was established, because district and circuit offices had a prison Sikong, "Grand" was again added.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sikong office was established, because county and circuit offices already had a prison officer called Sikong, "Grand" was added again.

sentences.zh: 王莽居攝，以漢無小司徒，而定司馬、司徒、司空之號並加大。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang held the regency, because Han had no lesser Situ, the titles Sima, Situ, and Sikong were fixed and all given the prefix "Grand."
translations.idiomatic: While Wang Mang held the regency, noting that Han lacked a lesser Situ, he fixed the titles Sima, Situ, and Sikong and prefixed each with "Grand."

sentences.zh: 光武建武二十七年，省大司馬，以太尉代之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu of Guangwu, Grand Commander-in-Chief was abolished and Grand Commandant replaced it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Jianwu, Emperor Guangwu abolished the Grand Commander-in-Chief and replaced it with the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初二年，復置大司馬，以曹仁居之，而太尉如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangchu of Emperor Wen of Wei, Grand Commander-in-Chief was restored, with Cao Ren holding it, while Grand Commandant remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen of Wei the Grand Commander-in-Chief was restored, with Cao Ren in the post, while the Grand Commandant continued as before.

sentences.zh: 大將軍，一人。

translations.literal: Grand General (Dajiangjun), one post.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General: one office.

sentences.zh: 凡將軍皆掌征伐。

translations.literal: All generals oversee campaigns and conquest.
translations.idiomatic: All generals were charged with campaigns and conquest.

sentences.zh: 周制，王立六軍。

translations.literal: Under Zhou institutions, the king established six armies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou institutions the king maintained six armies.

sentences.zh: 晉獻公作二軍，公將上軍。

translations.literal: Duke Xian of Jin created two armies; the duke himself commanded the upper army.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xian of Jin organized two armies; the duke himself led the upper army.

sentences.zh: 將軍之名，起於此也。

translations.literal: The name "general" (jiangjun) originated from this.
translations.idiomatic: The title of general originated in this practice.

sentences.zh: 楚懷王遣三將入關，宋義為上將。

translations.literal: King Huai of Chu sent three generals into the Pass; Song Yi was the supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: King Huai of Chu dispatched three generals to enter the Pass, with Song Yi as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 漢高帝以韓信為大將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaodi of Han made Han Xin Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han appointed Han Xin Grand General.

sentences.zh: 漢西京以大司馬冠之。

translations.literal: Western Han placed the title Grand Marshal above it.
translations.idiomatic: In Western Han, the title Grand Marshal was placed above it.

sentences.zh: 漢東京大將軍自為官，位在三司上。

translations.literal: Eastern Han made Grand General its own office, with rank above the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In Eastern Han the Grand General became an independent office, ranking above the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝青龍三年，晉宣帝自大將軍為太尉，然則大將軍在三司下矣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qinglong of Emperor Ming of Wei, the Duke of Jin was promoted from Grand General to Grand Commandant; thus the Grand General was below the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qinglong under Emperor Ming of Wei, when the Duke of Jin rose from Grand General to Grand Commandant, the Grand General's rank fell below the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 其後又在三司上。

translations.literal: Later it was again above the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward it rose again above the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 晉景帝為大將軍，而景帝叔父孚為太尉，奏改大將軍在太尉下，後還復舊。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing of Jin was Grand General, while his uncle Sima Fu was Grand Commandant; they memorialized to place the Grand General below the Grand Commandant, but later the former order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing of Jin served as Grand General while his uncle Sima Fu held the post of Grand Commandant, a memorial was submitted placing the Grand General below the Grand Commandant; later the old order was restored.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝踐阼，安平王孚為太宰，鄭沖為太傅，王祥為太保，義陽王望為太尉，何曾為司徒，荀顗為司空，石苞為大司馬，陳騫為大將軍，凡八公同時並置，唯無丞相焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Jin ascended the throne, Prince Fu of Anping was Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong was Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang was Grand Protector, Prince Wang of Yiyang was Grand Commandant, He Zeng was Minister over the Masses, Xun Yi was Minister of Works, Shi Bao was Grand Marshal, and Chen Qian was Grand General—eight dukes were established at the same time, but there was no Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Jin took the throne, eight great offices were filled at once: Prince Fu of Anping as Grand Preceptor, Zheng Chong as Grand Tutor, Wang Xiang as Grand Protector, Prince Wang of Yiyang as Grand Commandant, He Zeng as Minister over the Masses, Xun Yi as Minister of Works, Shi Bao as Grand Marshal, and Chen Qian as Grand General—with no Chancellor among them.

sentences.zh: 有蒼頭字宜祿。

translations.literal: There was a household servant whose courtesy name was Yilu.
translations.idiomatic: There was a household servant named Yilu.

sentences.zh: 至漢，丞相府每有所關白，到閤輒傳呼「宜祿」，以此為常。

translations.literal: By Han times, whenever the Chancellor's office had business to report, upon reaching the office gate they would always call out "Yilu"—this became customary.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times, whenever the Chancellor's office had a matter to report, the messenger would call out "Yilu" at the office gate, and this became standard practice.

sentences.zh: 丞相置三長史。

translations.literal: The Chancellor established three Chief Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor's office had three Chief Clerks.

sentences.zh: 丞相有疾，御史大夫率百僚三旦問起居，及瘳，詔遣尚書令若光祿大夫賜養牛，上尊酒。

translations.literal: When the Chancellor fell ill, the Grand Herald would lead the hundred officials to inquire after his health at dawn for three days; when he recovered, an edict would send the Director of the Masters of Writing or the Household Master of Splendor to grant an ox for nourishment and fine wine.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chancellor fell ill, the Grand Herald led all officials to inquire after him at dawn for three days running; upon his recovery, the throne would dispatch the Director of the Masters of Writing or the Household Master of Splendor with an ox for nourishment and fine wine.

sentences.zh: 漢景帝三公病，遣中黃門問病。

translations.literal: When the Three Excellencies fell ill under Emperor Jing of Han, the Court Yellow Gate was sent to inquire after their illness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Jing of Han, when one of the Three Excellencies fell ill, a Court Yellow Gate was sent to ask after him.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉則黃門郎，尤重者或侍中也。

translations.literal: In Wei and Jin it was the Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; for the most important cases, sometimes even the Attendant Within.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei and Jin it was a Gentleman of the Yellow Gate who was sent, and in the weightiest cases sometimes the Attendant Within himself.

sentences.zh: 魏武為丞相以來，置左右二長史而已。

translations.literal: From the time Cao Cao served as Chancellor, only two Chief Clerks, left and right, were established.
translations.idiomatic: From Cao Cao's tenure as Chancellor onward, only left and right Chief Clerks were appointed.

sentences.zh: 漢東京太傅府置掾、屬十人，御屬一人，令史十二人，不知皆何曹也。

translations.literal: The Eastern Han Grand Tutor's office established ten aides and subordinates, one imperial subordinate, and twelve clerks—their bureaus are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han's Grand Tutor's office had ten aides and subordinates, one imperial subordinate, and twelve clerks, though which bureaus they served is no longer known.

sentences.zh: 自太尉至大將軍、驃騎、車騎、衞將軍，皆有長史一人，將軍又各置司馬一人，太傅不置長史也。

translations.literal: From the Grand Commandant down to the Grand General, Fast Cavalry General, Chariots and Cavalry General, and Guard General, each had one Chief Clerk; each general also had one Marshal established separately; the Grand Tutor did not establish a Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: From the Grand Commandant through the Grand General, Fast Cavalry General, Chariots and Cavalry General, and Guard General, each office had one Chief Clerk, and each general also had a separate Marshal; the Grand Tutor's office had no Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 太尉府置掾、屬二十四人，西曹主府吏署用事，東曹主二千石長吏遷除事，戶曹主民戶祠祀農桑事，奏曹主奏議事，辭曹主辭訟事，法曹主郵驛科程事，尉曹主卒徒轉運事，賊曹主盜賊事，決曹主罪法事，兵曹主兵事，金曹主貨幣鹽鐵事，倉曹主倉穀事，黃閤主簿省錄眾事。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant's office established twenty-four aides and subordinates: the Western Bureau supervised the office staff and their duties; the Eastern Bureau supervised the appointment and removal of two-thousand-bushel officials; the Household Bureau supervised household registers, sacrifices, and farming and sericulture; the Memorial Bureau supervised memorials and deliberations; the Petition Bureau supervised petitions and lawsuits; the Law Bureau supervised postal relays, regulations, and procedures; the Commandant Bureau supervised convicts, corvée labor, and transport; the Bandit Bureau supervised theft and banditry; the Judgment Bureau supervised crimes and legal penalties; the Military Bureau supervised military affairs; the Revenue Bureau supervised currency, salt, and iron; the Granary Bureau supervised granaries and grain; the Yellow Chamber Chief Clerk supervised and recorded all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant's office had twenty-four aides and subordinates. The Western Bureau handled office personnel and administrative business; the Eastern Bureau handled appointments and dismissals of two-thousand-bushel officials; the Household Bureau handled population registers, sacrifices, and agriculture; the Memorial Bureau handled memorials and policy deliberations; the Petition Bureau handled petitions and litigation; the Law Bureau handled postal relays and regulatory procedures; the Commandant Bureau handled convicts, corvée transport, and labor relays; the Bandit Bureau handled theft and bandit cases; the Judgment Bureau handled crimes and penalties; the Military Bureau handled military affairs; the Revenue Bureau handled currency, salt, and iron; the Granary Bureau handled stores and grain; and the Yellow Chamber Chief Clerk supervised and recorded all office business.

sentences.zh: 御屬一人，令史二十二人。

translations.literal: One imperial subordinate and twenty-two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: There was one imperial subordinate and twenty-two clerks.

sentences.zh: 御屬主為公御，令史則有閤下、記室、門下令史，其餘史闕。

translations.literal: The imperial subordinate supervised service to the duke; among the clerks there were clerks of the office chamber, record chamber, and gate; the rest of the clerk positions are lost.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial subordinate oversaw the lord's personal attendants; among the clerks were those of the office chamber, record chamber, and gate, though the remaining clerk posts are no longer recorded.

sentences.zh: 案掾、屬二十四人，自東西曹凡十二曹，然則曹各置掾、屬一人，合二十四人也。

translations.literal: Examining the matter, the twenty-four aides and subordinates, from the Eastern and Western Bureaus through twelve bureaus in all—thus each bureau had one aide and one subordinate, totaling twenty-four persons.
translations.idiomatic: On examination, the twenty-four aides and subordinates correspond to twelve bureaus from the Eastern and Western Bureaus onward, with one aide and one subordinate in each bureau—twenty-four in all.

sentences.zh: 司徒置掾、屬三十一人，御屬一人，令史三十五人。

translations.literal: The Minister over the Masses established thirty-one aides and subordinates, one imperial subordinate, and thirty-five clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister over the Masses had thirty-one aides and subordinates, one imperial subordinate, and thirty-five clerks.

sentences.zh: 司空置掾二十九人，御屬一人，令史三十一人。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works established twenty-nine aides, one imperial subordinate, and thirty-one clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works had twenty-nine aides, one imperial subordinate, and thirty-one clerks.

sentences.zh: 司空別有道橋掾。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works separately had a Roads and Bridges aide.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works also had a separate aide for roads and bridges.

sentences.zh: 其餘張減之號，史闕不可得知也。

translations.literal: As for the rest, with the expansion and reduction of titles, the records are lost and cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: The rest, with titles added or removed over time, cannot be recovered from the incomplete records.

sentences.zh: 漢東京大將軍、驃騎將軍從事中郎二人，掾、屬二十九人，御屬一人，令史三十人。

translations.literal: Eastern Han's Grand General and Fast Cavalry General had two Attendant Gentlemen, twenty-nine aides and subordinates, one imperial subordinate, and thirty clerks.
translations.idiomatic: In Eastern Han, the Grand General and Fast Cavalry General each had two Attendant Gentlemen, twenty-nine aides and subordinates, one imperial subordinate, and thirty clerks.

sentences.zh: 騎、衞將軍從事中郎二人，掾、屬二十人，御屬一人，令史二十四人。

translations.literal: The Chariots and Cavalry General and Guard General had two Attendant Gentlemen, twenty aides and subordinates, one imperial subordinate, and twenty-four clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The Chariots and Cavalry General and Guard General each had two Attendant Gentlemen, twenty aides and subordinates, one imperial subordinate, and twenty-four clerks.

sentences.zh: 兵曹掾史主兵事，稟假掾史主稟假，又置外刺姦主罪法。

translations.literal: The Military Bureau aide-clerks supervised military affairs; the Rations and Leave aide-clerks supervised rations and leave; there was also an External Investigator of Wrongdoing supervising crimes and law.
translations.idiomatic: Military Bureau aide-clerks handled military affairs; Rations and Leave aide-clerks handled provisions and furloughs; and an External Investigator of Wrongdoing was also appointed to handle criminal law.

sentences.zh: 其領兵外討，則營有五部，部有校尉一人，軍司馬一人；

translations.literal: When leading troops on campaign abroad, the encampment had five sections; each section had one Commandant and one Army Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When commanding troops in the field, the encampment was divided into five sections, each with one Commandant and one Army Marshal.

sentences.zh: 部下有曲，曲有軍候一人；

translations.literal: Below each section were companies; each company had one Army Warder.
translations.idiomatic: Each section contained companies, each headed by an Army Warder.

sentences.zh: 曲下有屯，屯有屯長一人。

translations.literal: Below each company were platoons; each platoon had one Platoon Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Each company was subdivided into platoons, each commanded by a Platoon Chief.

sentences.zh: 若不置校尉，則部但有軍司馬一人。

translations.literal: If no Commandant was established, a section would have only one Army Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When no Commandant was appointed, a section had only an Army Marshal.

sentences.zh: 又有軍假司馬、軍假候，其別營者則為別部司馬。

translations.literal: There were also Acting Army Marshals and Acting Army Warders; for separate encampments there were Separate Section Marshals.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Acting Army Marshals and Acting Army Warders, and separate encampments had Separate Section Marshals.

sentences.zh: 其餘將軍置以征伐者，府無員職，亦有部曲司馬、軍候以領兵焉。

translations.literal: Other generals appointed for campaigns had no fixed staff in their offices, but also had section-and-company marshals and army warders to command troops.
translations.idiomatic: Other generals raised for campaigns had no permanent office staff, but still had section marshals and army warders to lead their troops.

sentences.zh: 案大將軍以下掾屬與三府張減，史闕不可得知。

translations.literal: Examining the Grand General and below, aides and subordinates were expanded and reduced along with the three offices; the records are lost and cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: Below the Grand General, aide and subordinate posts expanded and contracted with those of the three great offices, but the incomplete records leave the details unknown.

sentences.zh: 置令史、御屬者，則是同三府也。

translations.literal: Those that established clerks and imperial subordinates were the same as the three offices.
translations.idiomatic: Offices that included clerks and imperial subordinates matched the three great offices in structure.

sentences.zh: 其云掾史者，則是有掾而無屬，又無令史、御屬，不同三府也。

translations.literal: Those styled aide-clerks had aides but no subordinates, and also no clerks or imperial subordinates—different from the three offices.
translations.idiomatic: Posts styled aide-clerks had aides but no subordinates, and lacked clerks and imperial subordinates—unlike the three great offices.

sentences.zh: 魏初公府職僚，史不備書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wei, the staff of ducal offices was not fully recorded in history.
translations.idiomatic: In early Wei, the staff establishments of ducal offices were not fully documented.

sentences.zh: 及晉景帝為大將軍，置掾十人，西曹、東曹、戶曹、倉曹、賊曹、金曹、水曹、兵曹、騎兵各一人，則無屬矣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing of Jin became Grand General, ten aides were established—one each for the Western Bureau, Eastern Bureau, Household Bureau, Granary Bureau, Bandit Bureau, Revenue Bureau, Water Bureau, Military Bureau, and Cavalry—and there were no subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing served as Grand General, he appointed ten aides—one each for the Western, Eastern, Household, Granary, Bandit, Revenue, Water, Military, and Cavalry Bureaus—with no subordinates.

sentences.zh: 魏元帝咸熙中，晉文帝為相國，相國府置中衞將軍、驍騎將軍、左右長史、司馬、從事中郎四人，主簿四人，舍人十九人，參軍二十二人，參戰十一人，掾、屬三十三人。

translations.literal: In the Xianxi era of Emperor Yuan of Wei, when the Duke of Jin was Chancellor, the Chancellor's office established Guard General, Brave Cavalry General, left and right Chief Clerks, Marshals, four Attendant Gentlemen, four Chief Clerks, nineteen Masters of Reception, twenty-two Staff Officers, eleven Battle Staff Officers, and thirty-three aides and subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianxi era under Emperor Yuan of Wei, when the Duke of Jin served as Chancellor, his office included a Guard General, Brave Cavalry General, left and right Chief Clerks and Marshals, four Attendant Gentlemen, four Chief Clerks, nineteen Masters of Reception, twenty-two Staff Officers, eleven Battle Staff Officers, and thirty-three aides and subordinates.

sentences.zh: 東曹掾、屬各一人，西曹屬一人，戶曹掾一人，屬二人，賊曹掾一人，屬二人，金曹掾、屬各一人，兵曹掾、屬各一人，騎兵掾二人，屬一人，車曹掾、屬各一人，鎧曹掾、屬各一人，水曹掾、屬各一人，集曹掾、屬各一人，法曹掾、屬各一人，奏曹掾、屬各一人，倉曹屬二人，戎曹屬一人，馬曹屬一人，媒曹屬一人，合為三十三人。

translations.literal: The Eastern Bureau had one aide and one subordinate; the Western Bureau had one subordinate; the Household Bureau had one aide and two subordinates; the Bandit Bureau had one aide and two subordinates; the Revenue Bureau had one aide and one subordinate; the Military Bureau had one aide and one subordinate; the Cavalry Bureau had two aides and one subordinate; the Chariot Bureau had one aide and one subordinate; the Armor Bureau had one aide and one subordinate; the Water Bureau had one aide and one subordinate; the Assembly Bureau had one aide and one subordinate; the Law Bureau had one aide and one subordinate; the Memorial Bureau had one aide and one subordinate; the Granary Bureau had two subordinates; the Military Affairs Bureau had one subordinate; the Horse Bureau had one subordinate; the Matchmaking Bureau had one subordinate—totaling thirty-three persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Bureau had one aide and one subordinate; the Western Bureau one subordinate; the Household Bureau one aide and two subordinates; the Bandit Bureau one aide and two subordinates; the Revenue, Military, Chariot, Armor, Water, Assembly, Law, and Memorial Bureaus each one aide and one subordinate; the Cavalry Bureau two aides and one subordinate; the Granary Bureau two subordinates; and the Military Affairs, Horse, and Matchmaking Bureaus one subordinate each—thirty-three in all.

sentences.zh: 散屬九人，凡四十二人。

translations.literal: Nine unattached subordinates—in all forty-two persons.
translations.idiomatic: There were also nine unattached subordinates, for forty-two persons in all.

sentences.zh: 晉初凡位從公以上，置長史、西閤、東閤祭酒、西曹、東曹掾、戶曹、倉曹、賊曹屬各一人；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin, for all ranks from Secondary Duke upward, one Chief Clerk, Western Chamber Libationer, Eastern Chamber Libationer, and one subordinate each for the Western Bureau, Eastern Bureau, Household Bureau, Granary Bureau, and Bandit Bureau were established.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Jin, every office from Secondary Duke upward had one Chief Clerk, Western and Eastern Chamber Libationers, and one subordinate each for the Western, Eastern, Household, Granary, and Bandit Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 加兵者又置司馬、從事中郎、主簿、記室督各一人，舍人四人；

translations.literal: Those with added military authority also had one Marshal, Attendant Gentleman, Chief Clerk, and Record Chamber Supervisor each, and four Masters of Reception.
translations.idiomatic: Offices with military authority also had a Marshal, Attendant Gentleman, Chief Clerk, and Record Chamber Supervisor, plus four Masters of Reception.

sentences.zh: 為持節都督者，置參軍六人。

translations.literal: Those serving as Bearer of the Staff and Area Commander had six Staff Officers established.
translations.idiomatic: Area commanders bearing the imperial staff had six Staff Officers.

sentences.zh: 安平獻王孚為太宰，增掾、屬為十人，兵、鎧、士、營軍、刺姦五曹皆置屬，并前為十人也。

translations.literal: When Prince Fu of Anping, posthumously Prince Xian, was Grand Preceptor, aides and subordinates were increased to ten; the Military, Armor, Soldier, Camp Army, and Wrongdoing Investigation bureaus all had subordinates established—together with the earlier posts, ten persons.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xian of Anping served as Grand Preceptor, aides and subordinates were raised to ten, with subordinates added to the Military, Armor, Soldier, Camp Army, and Wrongdoing Investigation bureaus—for ten in all counting earlier posts.

sentences.zh: 楊駿為太傅，增祭酒為四人，掾、屬為二十人，兵曹分為左、右、法、金、田、集、水、戎、車、馬十曹，皆置屬，則為二十人。

translations.literal: When Yang Jun was Grand Tutor, libationers were increased to four and aides and subordinates to twenty; the Military Bureau was divided into Left, Right, Law, Revenue, Field, Assembly, Water, Military Campaign, Chariot, and Horse bureaus—ten bureaus all with subordinates established—for twenty persons.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jun served as Grand Tutor, libationers were increased to four and aides and subordinates to twenty; the Military Bureau was split into ten bureaus—Left, Right, Law, Revenue, Field, Assembly, Water, Military Campaign, Chariot, and Horse—each with a subordinate, twenty in all.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫為相國，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎四人，參軍二十人，主簿、記室督、祭酒各四人，掾、屬四十人。

translations.literal: When Prince Lun of Zhao was Chancellor, left and right Chief Clerks, Marshals, and four Attendant Gentlemen were established, twenty Staff Officers, four each of Chief Clerks, Record Chamber Supervisors, and Libationers, and forty aides and subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Lun of Zhao became Chancellor, the office had left and right Chief Clerks and Marshals, four Attendant Gentlemen, twenty Staff Officers, four Chief Clerks, four Record Chamber Supervisors, four Libationers, and forty aides and subordinates.

sentences.zh: 東西曹又置屬，其餘十八曹皆置掾，則四十人矣。

translations.literal: The Eastern and Western Bureaus also had subordinates established; the remaining eighteen bureaus all had aides established—for forty persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern and Western Bureaus also gained subordinates, and the other eighteen bureaus each had an aide—for forty in all.

sentences.zh: 凡諸曹皆置御屬、令史、學幹，御屬職錄事也。

translations.literal: All bureaus established imperial subordinates, clerks, and student clerks; the imperial subordinate's duty was to record affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Every bureau had imperial subordinates, clerks, and student clerks; the imperial subordinate's role was to keep records.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，諸公置長史、倉曹掾、戶曹屬、東西閤祭酒各一人，主簿、舍人二人，御屬二人，令史無定員。

translations.literal: Since the move to the left bank of the Yangzi, all dukes established one Chief Clerk, Granary Bureau aide, Household Bureau subordinate, and Eastern and Western Chamber Libationer each, two Chief Clerks and Masters of Reception, two imperial subordinates, and clerks with no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Since the court moved south of the Yangzi, each duke's office had one Chief Clerk, a Granary Bureau aide, a Household Bureau subordinate, one Eastern and one Western Chamber Libationer, two posts of Chief Clerk and Master of Reception, two imperial subordinates, and an unfixed number of clerks.

sentences.zh: 領兵者置司馬一人，從事中郎二人，參軍無定員；

translations.literal: Those commanding troops established one Marshal, two Attendant Gentlemen, and Staff Officers with no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders with troops had one Marshal, two Attendant Gentlemen, and an unfixed number of Staff Officers.

sentences.zh: 加崇者置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎四人，掾、屬四人，則倉曹增置屬，戶曹置掾，江左加崇，極於此也。

translations.literal: Those given added honor established left and right Chief Clerks, Marshals, and four Attendant Gentlemen, and four aides and subordinates; the Granary Bureau additionally had a subordinate established, and the Household Bureau had an aide established—added honor under Jiangzuo reached its limit here.
translations.idiomatic: The most highly honored also had left and right Chief Clerks and Marshals, four Attendant Gentlemen, and four aides and subordinates, with an extra Granary Bureau subordinate and a Household Bureau aide—the summit of added honor under the Southern Court.

sentences.zh: 長史、司馬、舍人，秦官。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk, Marshal, and Master of Reception were Qin offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Clerk, Marshal, and Master of Reception were Qin-dynasty offices.

sentences.zh: 從事中郎、掾、屬、主簿、令史，前漢官，陳湯為大將軍王鳳從事中郎是也。

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman, aide, subordinate, Chief Clerk, and clerk were Former Han offices—as when Chen Tang served as Attendant Gentleman to Grand General Wang Feng.
translations.idiomatic: The Attendant Gentleman, aide, subordinate, Chief Clerk, and clerk dated from Former Han, as when Chen Tang served as Attendant Gentleman to Grand General Wang Feng.

sentences.zh: 御屬、參軍，後漢官，孫堅為車騎參軍事是也。

translations.literal: Imperial subordinate and Staff Officer were Later Han offices—as when Sun Jian served as Chariots and Cavalry Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial subordinate and Staff Officer were Later Han offices, as when Sun Jian served as Staff Officer to the Chariots and Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 本於府主無敬，晉世太原孫楚為大司馬石苞參軍，輕慢苞，始制施敬。

translations.literal: Originally there was no deference owed to the lord of the office; in Jin times Sun Chu of Taiyuan was Staff Officer to Grand Marshal Shi Bao and treated Bao lightly—then regulations requiring deference were first established.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officers originally owed no ceremonial deference to their lord; in Jin, when Sun Chu of Taiyuan, staff officer to Grand Marshal Shi Bao, treated his lord with disrespect, regulations requiring deference were first imposed.

sentences.zh: 祭酒，晉官也，漢吳王濞為劉氏祭酒。

translations.literal: Libationer was a Jin office; in Han Prince Liu Bi of Wu served as Libationer for the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Libationer was a Jin office, though in Han Prince Liu Bi of Wu had served as clan Libationer.

sentences.zh: 夫祭祀以酒為本，長者主之，故以祭酒為稱。

translations.literal: Sacrifice takes wine as its foundation, and an elder presides—hence the title Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Since sacrifice is rooted in wine and presided over by an elder, the title Libationer derives from this.

sentences.zh: 漢之侍中、魏之散騎常侍高功者，並為祭酒焉。

translations.literal: Attendants Within of Han and Regular Attendants of the Cavalry-at-Large of high merit in Wei were both made Libationers.
translations.idiomatic: In Han the Attendant Within, and in Wei the senior Regular Attendant of the Cavalry-at-Large, could both hold the title of Libationer.

sentences.zh: 公府祭酒，蓋因其名也。

translations.literal: The ducal office Libationer probably derived its name from this.
translations.idiomatic: The ducal Libationer likely took its name from this tradition.

sentences.zh: 長史、從事中郎主吏，司馬主將，主簿、祭酒、舍人主閤內事，參軍、掾、屬、令史主諸曹事。

translations.literal: The Chief Clerk and Attendant Gentleman supervised officials; the Marshal supervised generals; the Chief Clerk, Libationer, and Master of Reception supervised inner-chamber affairs; Staff Officers, aides, subordinates, and clerks supervised the affairs of the various bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Clerk and Attendant Gentleman managed personnel; the Marshal handled military affairs; the Chief Clerk, Libationer, and Master of Reception managed inner-chamber business; and Staff Officers, aides, subordinates, and clerks handled the work of the bureaus.

sentences.zh: 司徒若無公，唯省舍人，其府常置，其職僚異於餘府。

translations.literal: If the Minister over the Masses had no duke incumbent, only the Master of Reception was omitted; the office itself was always maintained, and its staff differed from the other offices.
translations.idiomatic: When no duke held the post of Minister over the Masses, only the Master of Reception was dropped; the office itself remained permanent, with a staff structure unlike the other great offices.

sentences.zh: 有左右長史、左西曹掾、屬各一人，餘則同矣。

translations.literal: There were left and right Chief Clerks and one aide and one subordinate each for the Left Western Bureau; the rest were the same.
translations.idiomatic: It had left and right Chief Clerks and a Left Western Bureau aide and subordinate; otherwise it matched the others.

sentences.zh: 餘府有公則置，無則省。

translations.literal: The other offices established staff when there was a duke incumbent and omitted them when there was not.
translations.idiomatic: Other offices filled their staffs when a duke held the post and reduced them when none did.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝為鎮東大將軍及丞相，置從事中郎，無定員，分掌諸曹，有錄事中郎、度支中郎、三兵中郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Jin was Grand General Guarding the East and Chancellor, Attendant Gentlemen were established with no fixed quota to divide supervision of the bureaus among them—among them were Record Affairs Attendant Gentleman, Revenue Disbursement Attendant Gentleman, and Three Armies Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan served as Grand General Guarding the East and as Chancellor, he appointed Attendant Gentlemen without fixed numbers to oversee the bureaus, including Attendant Gentlemen for record-keeping, revenue disbursement, and the three armies.

sentences.zh: 其參軍則有諮議參軍二人，主諷議事，晉江左初置，因軍諮祭酒也，宋高祖為相，止置諮議參軍，無定員。

translations.literal: Among the Staff Officers there were two Advisory Staff Officers supervising deliberation and remonstrance; they were first established at the beginning of Jin south of the Yangzi, deriving from the Army Counsel Libationer; when Emperor Gaozu of Song was Chancellor, only Advisory Staff Officers were established, with no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: His Staff Officers included two Advisory Staff Officers who handled policy deliberation and remonstrance—first introduced when the Jin court moved south, evolving from the Army Counsel Libationer. When Emperor Gaozu of Song served as Chancellor, he retained only Advisory Staff Officers, with no fixed number.

sentences.zh: 今諸曹則有錄事、記室、戶曹、倉曹、中直兵、外兵、騎兵、長流賊曹、刑獄賊曹、城局賊曹、法曹、田曹、水曹、鎧曹、車曹、士曹、集、右戶、墨曹，凡十八曹參軍。

translations.literal: Now the bureaus have Record Affairs, Record Chamber, Household, Granary, Central Direct Military, External Military, Cavalry, Long-Term Pursuit Bandit, Criminal Prison Bandit, City Bureau Bandit, Law, Field, Water, Armor, Chariot, Soldier, Assembly, Right Household, and Ink bureaus—eighteen bureau Staff Officers in all.
translations.idiomatic: Today the bureaus include Staff Officers for record-keeping, the record chamber, household affairs, granaries, central and external military affairs, cavalry, long-term pursuit of bandits, criminal prisons, city defenses, law, fields, waterworks, armor, chariots, soldiers, assembly affairs, right household, and ink—eighteen bureau Staff Officers in all.

sentences.zh: 參軍不署曹者，無定員。

translations.literal: Staff Officers not assigned to a bureau had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Staff Officers without a bureau assignment had no fixed number.

sentences.zh: 江左初，晉元帝鎮東丞相府有錄事、記室、東曹、西曹、度支、戶曹、法曹、金曹、倉曹、理曹、中兵、外兵、騎兵、典兵、兵曹、賊曹、運曹、禁防、典賓、鎧曹、田曹、士曹、騎士、車曹參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiangzuo, Chancellor Yuan Di's office east of the river had Staff Officers for Record Affairs, Record Chamber, Eastern Bureau, Western Bureau, Revenue Disbursement, Household, Law, Revenue, Granary, Judicial, Central Military, External Military, Cavalry, Military Protocol, Military Bureau, Bandit, Transport, Guard and Defense, Ceremonial Reception, Armor, Field, Soldier, Cavalrymen, and Chariot bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: When the court first moved south, Grand Chancellor Yuan Di's eastern commandery office included Staff Officers for record-keeping, the record chamber, eastern and western bureaus, revenue disbursement, household affairs, law, revenue, granaries, judicial matters, central and external military affairs, cavalry, military protocol, the military bureau, bandit suppression, transport, guard and defense, ceremonial reception, armor, fields, soldiers, cavalrymen, and chariots.

sentences.zh: 其東曹、西曹、度支、金曹、理曹、典兵、兵曹、賊曹、運曹、禁防、典賓、騎士、車曹凡十三曹，今闕所餘十二曹也。

translations.literal: Of these, the Eastern Bureau, Western Bureau, Revenue Disbursement, Revenue, Judicial, Military Protocol, Military Bureau, Bandit, Transport, Guard and Defense, Ceremonial Reception, Cavalrymen, and Chariot bureaus—thirteen bureaus in all—are now absent; the remaining twelve bureaus survive.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen of these bureaus—the Eastern and Western Bureaus, Revenue Disbursement, Revenue, Judicial Affairs, Military Protocol, Military Bureau, Bandit Suppression, Transport, Guard and Defense, Ceremonial Reception, Cavalrymen, and Chariots—have since been dropped, leaving twelve.

sentences.zh: 其後又有直兵、長流、刑獄、城局、水曹、右戶、墨曹七曹。

translations.literal: Later there were also seven bureaus: Direct Military, Long-Term Pursuit, Criminal Prison, City Bureau, Water, Right Household, and Ink.
translations.idiomatic: Seven more were added later: Direct Military, Long-Term Pursuit, Criminal Prison, City Bureau, Water, Right Household, and Ink.

sentences.zh: 高祖為相，合中兵、直兵置一參軍，曹則猶二也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was Chancellor, Central Military and Direct Military were combined under one Staff Officer, though the bureaus remained two.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu served as Chancellor, he merged the Central and Direct Military bureaus under one Staff Officer, though the two bureaus themselves remained separate.

sentences.zh: 今小府不置長流參軍者，置禁防參軍。

translations.literal: Now smaller offices that do not establish a Long-Term Pursuit Staff Officer establish a Guard and Defense Staff Officer instead.
translations.idiomatic: Smaller offices that lack a Long-Term Pursuit Staff Officer appoint a Guard and Defense Staff Officer in its place.

sentences.zh: 蜀丞相諸葛亮府有行參軍，晉太傅司馬越府又有行參軍、兼行參軍，後漸加長兼字，除拜則為參軍事，府板則為行參軍。

translations.literal: Chancellor Zhuge Liang of Shu had Acting Staff Officers; Grand Tutor Sima Yue of Jin also had Acting Staff Officers and Concurrent Acting Staff Officers; later the terms "long" and "concurrent" were gradually added—imperial appointment made one a Staff Officer, while office commission made one an Acting Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhuge Liang of Shu employed Acting Staff Officers; Grand Tutor Sima Yue's office added Acting and Concurrent Acting Staff Officers; over time the titles acquired "long" and "concurrent" qualifiers—imperial appointment conferred full Staff Officer status, while an office commission conferred Acting Staff Officer status.

sentences.zh: 晉末以來，參軍事、行參軍又各有除板。

translations.literal: From the end of Jin onward, Staff Officers and Acting Staff Officers each had separate imperial appointments and office commissions.
translations.idiomatic: From late Jin onward, full Staff Officers and Acting Staff Officers each had distinct paths of imperial appointment and office commission.

sentences.zh: 板行參軍下則長兼行參軍。

translations.literal: Below an office-commissioned Acting Staff Officer was the Long Concurrent Acting Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Below an office-commissioned Acting Staff Officer ranked the Long Concurrent Acting Staff Officer.

sentences.zh: 參軍督護，江左置，本皆領營，有部曲，今則無矣。

translations.literal: Staff Officer Commandant-Protector was established under Jiangzuo; originally all commanded camps and had personal troops—now they do not.
translations.idiomatic: The Staff Officer Commandant-Protector was a Jiangzuo appointment; such officers once commanded camps with personal retinues, but no longer do.

sentences.zh: 公府長史、司馬，秩千石；

translations.literal: Chief Clerks and Marshals of ducal offices had rank of one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerks and Marshals of ducal offices ranked at one thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 從事中郎，六百石；

translations.literal: Attendant Gentlemen, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Gentlemen ranked at six hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 東西曹掾，四百石；

translations.literal: Eastern and Western Bureau aides, four hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern and Western Bureau aides ranked at four hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 他掾三百石；

translations.literal: Other aides, three hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: All other aides ranked at three hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 屬二百石。

translations.literal: Subordinates, two hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates ranked at two hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 特進，前漢世所置，前後二漢及魏、晉以為加官，從本官車服，無吏卒。

translations.literal: Special Advancement was established in Former Han; Former and Later Han and Wei and Jin used it as an added honor, following the carriage and insignia of one's original office, with no clerks or servants.
translations.idiomatic: Special Advancement was an office of Former Han; in both Han dynasties and under Wei and Jin it served as an honorary add-on, conferring no staff of its own while preserving the carriage and insignia of one's substantive post.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康中定位令在諸公下，驃騎將軍上。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era of Emperor Hui of Jin the rank order was fixed below the dukes and above the Fast Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Hui's Yuankang era, its rank was fixed below the dukes and above the Fast Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍，一人。

translations.literal: Fast Cavalry General, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Fast Cavalry General: one post.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝元狩二年，始用霍去病為驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanshou of Emperor Wu of Han, Huo Qubing was first made Fast Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu of Han, Huo Qubing became the first Fast Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 漢西京制，大將軍、驃騎將軍位次丞相。

translations.literal: Under Western Han regulations, the Grand General and Fast Cavalry General ranked next after the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Western Han practice, the Grand General and Fast Cavalry General ranked immediately below the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍，一人。

translations.literal: Chariots and Cavalry General, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Chariots and Cavalry General: one post.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝元年，始用薄昭為車騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Wen of Han, Bo Zhao was first made Chariots and Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Wen's reign, Bo Zhao became the first Chariots and Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 魚豢曰：「魏世車騎為都督，儀與四征同。

translations.literal: Yu Huan says: "In Wei times, when the Chariots and Cavalry General served as Area Commander, his ceremonial insignia matched the Four Expanding Generals.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Huan writes: "In Wei, a Chariots and Cavalry General serving as area commander enjoyed ceremonial parity with the Four Expanding Generals.

sentences.zh: 若不為都督，雖持節屬四征者，與前後左右雜號將軍同。

translations.literal: If not serving as Area Commander, even if bearing the staff and subordinate to a Four Expanding General, he ranked with the Front, Rear, Left, Right, and miscellaneous-title generals.
translations.idiomatic: When not serving as area commander, even one bearing the staff under a Four Expanding General ranked with the Front, Rear, Left, Right, and miscellaneous-title generals.

sentences.zh: 其或散還從文官之例，則位次三司。」

translations.literal: If dismissed and returned to follow the civil-official precedent, he ranked next after the Three Excellencies."
translations.idiomatic: If discharged and restored to civil rank, he took his place below the Three Excellencies."

sentences.zh: 晉、宋車騎、衞不復為四征所督也。

translations.literal: Under Jin and Song, Chariots and Cavalry and Guard generals were no longer supervised by the Four Expanding Generals.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin and Song, the Chariots and Cavalry and Guard generals were no longer placed under the Four Expanding Generals.

sentences.zh: 衞將軍，一人。

translations.literal: Guard General, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Guard General: one post.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝元年，始用宋昌為衞將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Wen of Han, Song Chang was first made Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Wen's reign, Song Chang became the first Guard General.

sentences.zh: 三號位亞三司。

translations.literal: The three titled generals ranked next below the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: The three great generals ranked just below the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 漢章帝建初三年，始使車騎將軍馬防班同三司。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianchu of Emperor Zhang of Han, Chariots and Cavalry General Ma Fang was first granted ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianchu under Emperor Zhang of Han, Chariots and Cavalry General Ma Fang was the first granted ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 班同三司自此始也。

translations.literal: Ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies dates from this grant.

sentences.zh: 漢末奮威將軍，晉江右伏波、輔國將軍，並加大而儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the end of Han the Inspiring Awe General; under Jin west of the river the Wave-Quelling and State-Supporting generals—all had "Grand" added to the title with ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han came the Inspiring Awe General; under Jin west of the Yangzi the Wave-Quelling and State-Supporting generals—all received the prefix "Grand" and ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，將軍則中、鎮、撫、四鎮以上或加大，餘官則左右光祿大夫以上並得儀同三司，自此以下不得也。

translations.literal: Since the Jiangzuo period, for generals the Central Army, Army Garrisoning, Army Pacifying, and Four Regional Pacification Generals and above sometimes had "Grand" added to the title; for other offices those from Left and Right Grandees of Splendid Happiness upward all might receive ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies—those below this could not.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jiangzuo period, generals from the Central Army, Army Garrisoning, Army Pacifying, and Four Regional Pacification ranks upward sometimes received the prefix "Grand"; other offices from Left and Right Grandees of Splendid Happiness upward could all receive ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, but ranks below could not.

sentences.zh: 持節都督，無定員。

translations.literal: Area Commander with Staff of Authority: no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Area Commanders with Staff of Authority had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 前漢遣使，始有持節。

translations.literal: When Former Han dispatched envoys, bearing the staff first appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Former Han first introduced the staff of authority when dispatching envoys.

sentences.zh: 光武建武初，征伐四方，始權時置督軍御史，事竟罷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu under Emperor Guangwu, campaigning in all directions, Army-Supervising Censors were first established on a temporary basis and abolished when the affair was concluded.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jianwu era, as Emperor Guangwu campaigned in all directions, Army-Supervising Censors were first established on a temporary basis and disbanded once the campaigns ended.

sentences.zh: 建安中，魏武帝為相，始遣大將軍督軍。

translations.literal: During the Jian'an era, when Duke Cao of Wei served as Chancellor, Grand Generals were first dispatched to supervise armies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jian'an era, after Duke Cao of Wei became Chancellor, Grand Generals were first sent out to supervise armies.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，征孫權還，夏侯惇督二十六軍是也。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, returning from the campaign against Sun Quan, Xiahou Dun supervised twenty-six armies—this was such a case.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, on returning from the campaign against Sun Quan, Xiahou Dun supervised twenty-six armies; this was one such appointment.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初二年，始置都督諸州軍事，或領刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen of Wei, Area Commanders of military affairs in the various provinces were first established; some also held the post of Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen of Wei, provincial area commanders of military affairs were first established, some concurrently serving as Inspector.

sentences.zh: 三年，上軍大將軍曹真都督中外諸軍事，假黃鉞，則總統外內諸軍矣。

translations.literal: In the third year, Upper Army Grand General Cao Zhen served as area commander of all military affairs inside and outside the capital; granted the conferred Yellow Axe, he then commanded all armies at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Upper Army Grand General Cao Zhen became area commander of all military affairs inside and outside the capital; once granted the conferred Yellow Axe, he commanded all armies at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 明帝太和四年，晉宣帝征蜀，加號大都督。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe under Emperor Ming, when the Duke of Jin campaigned against Shu, the title Great Area Commander was added.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe under Emperor Ming, when the Duke of Jin campaigned against Shu, he received the added title Great Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 高貴公正元二年，晉文帝都督中外諸軍，尋加大都督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengyuan under the Deposed Emperor of Wei, the Duke of Jin commanded all armies inside and outside the capital; soon afterward he was promoted to Great Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengyuan under the Deposed Emperor of Wei, the Duke of Jin took command of all armies inside and outside the capital and was soon promoted to Great Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 晉世則都督諸軍為上，監諸軍次之，督諸軍為下。

translations.literal: In Jin times, Commanding All Armies ranked highest, Supervising All Armies next, and Directing All Armies lowest.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin, Commanding All Armies ranked highest, Supervising All Armies came next, and Directing All Armies ranked lowest.

sentences.zh: 使持節為上，持節次之，假節為下。

translations.literal: Commissioner Bearing the Staff ranked highest, Bearer of the Staff next, and Acting Bearer of the Staff lowest.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Bearing the Staff ranked highest, Bearer of the Staff came next, and Acting Bearer of the Staff ranked lowest.

sentences.zh: 使持節得殺二千石以下；

translations.literal: A Commissioner Bearing the Staff might execute officials of two-thousand-dan rank and below;
translations.idiomatic: A Commissioner Bearing the Staff could execute officials of two-thousand-dan rank and below;

sentences.zh: 持節殺無官位人，若軍事得與使持節同；

translations.literal: a Bearer of the Staff might kill men without official rank; in military affairs authority matched the Commissioner Bearer of the Staff;
translations.idiomatic: a Bearer of the Staff could kill men without official rank, and in military affairs held the same authority as a Commissioner Bearer of the Staff;

sentences.zh: 假節唯軍事得殺犯軍令者。

translations.literal: an Acting Bearer of the Staff might execute only those who violated military orders.
translations.idiomatic: an Acting Bearer of the Staff could execute only those who violated military orders.

sentences.zh: 晉江左以來，都督中外尤重，唯王導居之。

translations.literal: Since Jin east of the Yangzi, commanding all armies inside and outside the capital was especially weighty; only Wang Dao held it.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jin east of the Yangzi, command of all armies inside and outside the capital was especially exalted; only Wang Dao held that post.

sentences.zh: 宋氏人臣則無也。

translations.literal: Under the Song there was none among ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Liu Song no minister held it.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭假黃鉞。

translations.literal: Prince Yigong of Jiangxia received the conferred Yellow Axe.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yigong of Jiangxia was granted the conferred Yellow Axe.

sentences.zh: 假黃鉞，則專戮節將，非人臣常器矣。

translations.literal: When granted the conferred Yellow Axe, one held exclusive power to execute generals bearing the staff—it was not a minister's ordinary instrument.
translations.idiomatic: The conferred Yellow Axe conferred exclusive power to execute staff-bearing generals; it was not an instrument ordinarily held by ministers.

sentences.zh: 征東將軍，一人。

translations.literal: Eastern Expeditionary General, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Expeditionary General: one post.

sentences.zh: 漢獻帝初平三年，馬騰居之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chuping under Emperor Xian of Han, Ma Teng held it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chuping under Emperor Xian of Han, Ma Teng held the post.

sentences.zh: 征南將軍，一人。

translations.literal: Southern Expeditionary General, one person.

translations.idiomatic: Traversing Wilds was held by Geng Chun.

translations.idiomatic: Sweeping Bandits was held by Man Chong during the Jian'an era under Han.

sentences.zh: 虎威，于禁居之。

translations.idiomatic: Tiger Awe was held by Yu Jin.

sentences.zh: 其餘或是後漢及魏所置，今則或置或不。

translations.literal: The rest were perhaps established in Later Han and Wei; now some are appointed and some are not.
translations.idiomatic: The rest were perhaps established in Later Han and Wei; under the present dynasty some are appointed and some are not.

sentences.zh: 自左右前後將軍以下至此四十號，唯四中郎將各一人，餘皆無定員。

translations.literal: From the Left, Right, Front, and Rear Generals down through these forty titles, only the four Palace Guard Generals had one post each; the rest had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: From the Left, Right, Front, and Rear Generals down through these forty titles, only the four Palace Guard Generals had one post each; all the rest had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 自車騎以下為刺史又都督及儀同三司者，置官如領兵，但云都督不儀同三司者，不置從事中郎，置功曹一人，主吏，在主簿上，漢末官也。

translations.literal: From Chariots and Cavalry downward, those who served as Inspector and area commander and held ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies established offices as when commanding troops; where one was merely area commander without ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, no Attendant Gentleman was established, but one Merit Officer was established to head clerks, ranking above the Chief Recorder—an office of late Han.
translations.idiomatic: From Chariots and Cavalry downward, those who served concurrently as Inspector and area commander and held ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies staffed their offices as commanders of troops did; where one served only as area commander without ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, no Attendant Gentleman was appointed, but a single Merit Officer was appointed to head the clerks, ranking above the Chief Recorder—a late Han office.

sentences.zh: 漢東京司隸有功曹從事史，如諸州治中，因其名也。

translations.literal: Eastern Han's Metropolitan Intendant had a Merit Officer Attendant Clerk, like a provincial Chief Controller—on this account came the name.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han's Metropolitan Intendant had a Merit Officer Attendant Clerk, comparable to a provincial Chief Controller; the title derives from that office.

sentences.zh: 功曹參軍一人，主佐□□記室下，戶曹上。

translations.literal: One Merit Officer Military Advisor, who assists and supports [text lost], ranking below the Record Chamber Staff Officer and above the Household Bureau Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Merit Officer Military Advisor, who assisted the chief clerks and ranked below the Record Chamber Staff Officer but above the Household Bureau Staff Officer.

sentences.zh: 監以下不置諮議、記室，餘則同矣。

translations.literal: Below Supervising All Armies, Advisory and Record Chamber posts were not established; the rest was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Below the rank of Supervising All Armies, no Advisory or Record Chamber Staff Officers were appointed; otherwise the staffing was the same.

sentences.zh: 宋太宗已來，皇子、皇弟雖非都督，亦置記室參軍。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Taizong of Song, imperial princes and younger imperial brothers, though not area commanders, also had Record Chamber Staff Officers established.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Taizong of Song, imperial princes and younger imperial brothers were also given Record Chamber Staff Officers even when they did not serve as area commanders.

sentences.zh: 小號將軍為大郡邊守置佐吏者，又置長史，餘則同也。

translations.literal: Minor-title generals serving as border commanders of great commanderies who were given staff also had Chief Clerks established; the rest was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Minor-title generals who served as frontier administrators of major commanderies and were granted a staff also received Chief Clerks; in other respects the arrangement was the same.

sentences.zh: 太常

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Ceremonies

sentences.zh: 太常，一人。

translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Ceremonies: one post.

sentences.zh: 舜攝帝位，命伯夷作秩宗，掌三禮，即其任也。

translations.literal: When Shun acted as regent, he appointed Boyi Minister of Rank to oversee the three rites—this was the origin of the office.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun served as regent he appointed Boyi Minister of Rank to oversee the three rites; that was the origin of this office.

sentences.zh: 周時曰宗伯，是為春官，掌邦禮。

translations.literal: In Zhou times it was called Minister of Ancestral Ritual; this was the Spring Minister, overseeing the rites of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou it was called Minister of Ancestral Ritual, the Spring Minister charged with the rites of the realm.

sentences.zh: 秦改曰奉常，漢因之。

translations.literal: Qin changed the name to Director of Ceremonial Observance, and Han followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Qin renamed the office Director of Ceremonial Observance, and Han retained the title.

sentences.zh: 景帝中六年，更名曰太常。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the middle Jingdi reign, the name was again changed to Grand Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the middle reign of Emperor Jing the office was renamed Grand Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 應劭曰：「欲令國家盛大常存，故稱太常。」

translations.literal: Ying Shao says: "They wished to have the state flourish grandly and endure forever, hence the name Grand Minister of Ceremonies."
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao writes: "They wished the state to flourish grandly and endure forever, hence the title Grand Minister of Ceremonies."

sentences.zh: 前漢常以列侯忠孝敬慎者居之，後漢不必列侯也。

translations.literal: In Former Han marquises who were loyal, respectful, and prudent usually held it; in Later Han a marquis title was not required.
