translations.idiomatic: In Former Han the post was usually held by marquises noted for loyalty, respect, and prudence; in Later Han a marquis title was no longer required.

sentences.zh: 博士，班固云，秦官。

translations.literal: Erudite: Ban Gu says it was a Qin office.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite: Ban Gu states that this was a Qin office.

sentences.zh: 史臣案，六國時往往有博士，掌通古今。

translations.literal: The recorder notes that in the Warring States era erudites were often found, overseeing mastery of past and present.
translations.idiomatic: The recorder notes that erudites were already common in the Warring States period, charged with mastery of past and present learning.

sentences.zh: 漢武建元五年，初置五經博士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jianyuan under Emperor Wu of Han, erudites of the Five Classics were first established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jianyuan under Emperor Wu of Han the first erudites of the Five Classics were appointed.

sentences.zh: 宣、成之世，五經家法稍增，經置博士一人。

translations.literal: In the reigns of Emperors Xuan and Cheng, the schools of the Five Classics gradually increased, and one erudite was established for each classic.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Xuan and Cheng the schools of the Five Classics gradually multiplied until each classic had its own erudite.

sentences.zh: 至東京凡十四人。

translations.literal: By the Eastern Capital there were fourteen in all.
translations.idiomatic: By the Later Han capital there were fourteen in all.

sentences.zh: 易，施、孟、梁丘、京氏；

translations.literal: Changes: the Shi, Meng, Liangqiu, and Jing schools;
translations.idiomatic: Changes: the Shi, Meng, Liangqiu, and Jing schools;

sentences.zh: 尚書，歐陽、大小夏侯；

translations.literal: Documents: Ouyang and the Greater and Lesser Xiahou schools;
translations.idiomatic: Documents: the Ouyang and Greater and Lesser Xiahou schools;

sentences.zh: 詩，齊、魯、韓；

translations.literal: Odes: the Qi, Lu, and Han schools;
translations.idiomatic: Odes: the Qi, Lu, and Han schools;

sentences.zh: 禮，大小戴；

translations.literal: Rites: the Greater and Lesser Dai schools;
translations.idiomatic: Rites: the Greater and Lesser Dai schools;

sentences.zh: 春秋，嚴、顏：各一博士。

translations.literal: Spring and Autumn: the Yan and Yan schools—one erudite for each.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and Autumn: the Yan and Yan schools, one erudite for each.

sentences.zh: 而聰明有威重者一人為祭酒。

translations.literal: Among them, one who was intelligent and possessed weight and authority served as Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: One erudite who was intelligent and commanding in bearing served as Libationer.

sentences.zh: 魏及晉西朝置十九人，江左初減為九人，皆不知掌何經。

translations.literal: Under Wei and the Western Jin court nineteen were established; at the beginning of the southward court the number was reduced to nine, with no assignment to any particular classic known.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei and the Western Jin court there were nineteen posts; when the court first moved south the number fell to nine, and none were assigned to a specific classic.

sentences.zh: 元帝末，增儀禮、春秋公羊博士各一人，合為十一人。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Yuan's reign, one erudite each for Ceremonial Rites and the Gongyang Commentary on Spring and Autumn was added, making eleven in all.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Yuan's reign one erudite each for Ceremonial Rites and the Gongyang Commentary on Spring and Autumn was added, bringing the total to eleven.

sentences.zh: 後又增為十六人，不復分掌五經，而謂之太學博士也。

translations.literal: Later the number was again increased to sixteen; they no longer divided supervision of the Five Classics among themselves, and were called Imperial Academy Erudites.
translations.idiomatic: Later the corps was expanded again to sixteen and no longer divided by classic; these officers were called Imperial Academy Erudites.

sentences.zh: 秩六百石。

translations.literal: Rank of six hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: Their rank was six hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒一人，國子博士二人，國子助教十人。

translations.literal: One Libationer of the Imperial Academy, two Imperial Academy Erudites, and ten Imperial Academy Assistants.
translations.idiomatic: There were one Libationer of the Imperial Academy, two Imperial Academy Erudites, and ten Imperial Academy Assistants.

sentences.zh: 周易、尚書、毛詩、禮記、周官、儀禮、春秋左氏傳、公羊、穀梁各為一經，論語、孝經為一經，合十經。

translations.literal: Zhou Changes, Documents, Mao Odes, Record of Rites, Rites of Zhou, Ceremonial Rites, Zuo Commentary on Spring and Autumn, Gongyang, and Guliang each counted as one classic; Analects and Classic of Filial Piety counted as one classic—ten classics in all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Changes, Documents, Mao Odes, Record of Rites, Rites of Zhou, Ceremonial Rites, Zuo Commentary on Spring and Autumn, Gongyang, and Guliang each formed one classic, while Analects and Classic of Filial Piety together formed another, making ten classics in all.

sentences.zh: 助教分掌。

translations.literal: The assistants divided supervision among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The assistants divided the classics among themselves.

sentences.zh: 國子，周舊名，周有師氏之職，即今國子祭酒也。

translations.literal: Imperial Academy is an old Zhou name; Zhou had the office of Master, which is today's Libationer of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Academy is an old Zhou name; the Zhou office of Master corresponds to today's Libationer of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 晉初復置國子學，以教生徒，而隸屬太學焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin the Imperial Academy was restored to instruct students, and was subordinate to the Imperial Academy proper.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Jin the Imperial Academy school was restored to instruct students and was placed under the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 晉初助教十五人，江左以來，損其員。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin there were fifteen assistants; since the court moved south the quota was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Jin there were fifteen assistants; since the court moved south their number was reduced.

sentences.zh: 自宋世若不置學，則助教唯置一人，而祭酒、博士常置也。

translations.literal: From Song times, if the school was not established, only one assistant was appointed, while the Libationer and erudites were always kept.
translations.idiomatic: From Song times, when the school itself was not established only one assistant was appointed, but the Libationer and erudites were always retained.

sentences.zh: 太廟令，一人。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 並前漢置。

translations.literal: Both were established in Former Han.
translations.idiomatic: Both posts dated from Former Han.

sentences.zh: 西京曰長，東京曰令。

translations.literal: In the Western Capital the title was Chief; in the Eastern Capital it was Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the Western Capital the title was Chief; in the Eastern Capital it was Director.

sentences.zh: 領齋郎二十四人。

translations.literal: He oversaw twenty-four Purification Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The office oversaw twenty-four Purification Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 明堂令，一人。

translations.literal: Director of the Bright Hall, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Bright Hall: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 丞，漢東京初置，令，宋世祖大明中置。

translations.literal: The assistant director was first established in Later Han's Eastern Capital; the director was established in the Daming era under Emperor Shizu of Song.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant director was first established under Later Han; the director was added in the Daming era under Emperor Shizu of Song.

sentences.zh: 太祝令，一人。

translations.literal: Director of the Grand Invocator, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Grand Invocator: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 掌祭祀讀祝迎送神。

translations.literal: He oversaw sacrifices, reading invocations, and receiving and sending off the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The office oversaw sacrifices, the reading of invocations, and the receiving and sending off of the spirits.

sentences.zh: 太祝，周舊官也。

translations.literal: Grand Invocator was an old Zhou office.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Invocator was an ancient Zhou office.

sentences.zh: 漢西京置太祝令、丞，武帝太初元年，更名曰廟祀。

translations.literal: Former Han's Western Capital established the Director and Assistant Director of the Grand Invocator; in the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu the name was changed to Temple Sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Former Han's Western Capital established the Director and Assistant Director of the Grand Invocator; in the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu the office was renamed Temple Sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 漢東京改曰太祝。

translations.literal: Later Han's Eastern Capital changed the name back to Grand Invocator.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han's Eastern Capital restored the title Grand Invocator.

sentences.zh: 太史令，一人。

translations.literal: Director of the Grand Astrologer, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Grand Astrologer: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 掌三辰時日祥瑞妖災，歲終則奏新曆。

translations.literal: He oversaw the three luminaries, days and seasons, auspicious omens, and calamities and portents; at year's end he presented the new calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The office oversaw the three luminaries, days and seasons, auspicious omens, and calamities and portents, and at year's end presented the new calendar.

sentences.zh: 太史，三代舊官，周世掌建邦之六典，正歲年，以序事頒朔于邦國。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer was an old office of the Three Dynasties; in Zhou times he oversaw the six canons for governing the state, rectified the year, ordered affairs, and distributed the calendar throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer was an ancient office of the Three Dynasties; under Zhou he kept the six canons for governing the state, rectified the year, ordered affairs, and distributed the calendar throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 又有馮相氏，掌天文次序；

translations.literal: There was also the Director of Celestial Patterns, overseeing the order of astronomy;
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Director of Celestial Patterns, who oversaw the order of the heavens;

sentences.zh: 保章氏，掌天文。

translations.literal: the Director of Celestial Archivists, overseeing astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: and the Director of Celestial Archivists, who oversaw astronomy.

sentences.zh: 今之太史，則并周之太史、馮相、保章三職也。

translations.literal: Today's Grand Astrologer combines the three Zhou offices of Grand Astrologer, Director of Celestial Patterns, and Director of Celestial Archivists.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Grand Astrologer combined the three Zhou offices of Grand Astrologer, Director of Celestial Patterns, and Director of Celestial Archivists.

sentences.zh: 漢西京曰太史令。

translations.literal: Former Han's Western Capital called it Director of the Grand Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: Former Han's Western Capital called the office Director of the Grand Astrologer.

sentences.zh: 漢東京有二丞，其一在靈臺。

translations.literal: Later Han's Eastern Capital had two assistant directors, one of them at the Spirit Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han's Eastern Capital had two assistant directors, one stationed at the Spirit Terrace.

sentences.zh: 太樂令，一人。

translations.literal: Director of Grand Music, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Grand Music: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 掌凡諸樂事。

translations.literal: He oversaw all music affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The office oversaw all musical affairs.

sentences.zh: 周時為大司樂。

translations.literal: In Zhou times it was Grand Minister of Music.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou it was Grand Minister of Music.

sentences.zh: 漢西京曰太樂令。

translations.literal: Former Han's Western Capital called it Director of Grand Music.
translations.idiomatic: Former Han's Western Capital called the office Director of Grand Music.

sentences.zh: 漢東京曰大予樂令。

translations.literal: Later Han's Eastern Capital called it Director of Grand Nurture Music.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han's Eastern Capital called it Director of Grand Nurture Music.

sentences.zh: 魏復為太樂令。

translations.literal: Under Wei it was again Director of Grand Music.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei the title reverted to Director of Grand Music.

sentences.zh: 陵令，每陵各一人。

translations.literal: Tomb Director: one for each tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb Director: one for each imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 漢舊官也。

translations.literal: It was an old Han office.
translations.idiomatic: This was an old Han office.

sentences.zh: 乘黃令，一人。

translations.literal: Director of the Yellow Harness, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Yellow Harness: one post.

sentences.zh: 掌乘輿車及安車諸馬。

translations.literal: He oversaw the imperial carriage and the horses of comfort carriages.
translations.idiomatic: The office oversaw the imperial carriage and the horses of the comfort carriages.

sentences.zh: 魏世置。

translations.literal: It was established in Wei times.
translations.idiomatic: The office was established under Wei.

sentences.zh: 自博士至乘黃令，並屬太常。

translations.literal: From the Erudites down to the Director of the Yellow Harness, all were subordinate to the Grand Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: From the Erudites down to the Director of the Yellow Harness, all were subordinate to the Grand Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: ====光祿勳，一人。

translations.literal: Director of Attendants, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Attendants: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 光，明也。

translations.literal: Guang means brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Guang means brightness.

sentences.zh: 祿，爵也。

translations.literal: Lu means stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Lu means stipend.

sentences.zh: 勳，功也。

translations.literal: Xun means merit.
translations.idiomatic: Xun means merit.

sentences.zh: 秦曰郎中令，漢因之。

translations.literal: Qin called it Director of Palace Gentlemen, and Han followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Qin called the office Director of Palace Gentlemen, and Han retained the title.

sentences.zh: 漢武太初元年，更名光祿勳。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu of Han, the name was changed to Director of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu of Han the office was renamed Director of Attendants.

sentences.zh: 掌三署郎，郎執戟衞宮殿門戶。

translations.literal: He oversaw the gentlemen of the Three Bureaus; the gentlemen bore halberds and guarded the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: The office oversaw the gentlemen of the Three Bureaus, who bore halberds and guarded the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 光祿勳居禁中如御史，有獄在殿門外，謂之光祿外部。

translations.literal: The Director of Attendants resided within the Forbidden precinct like the Censor, and had a prison outside the palace gate called the Outer Office of the Director of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Attendants dwelt within the Forbidden precinct like the Censor and maintained a prison outside the palace gate called the Outer Office of the Director of Attendants.

sentences.zh: 光祿勳郊祀掌三獻。

translations.literal: At suburban sacrifices the Director of Attendants oversaw the three libations.
translations.idiomatic: At suburban sacrifices the Director of Attendants performed the three libations.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以來，光祿勳不復居禁中，又無復三署郎，唯外宮朝會，則以名到焉。

translations.literal: Since Wei and Jin, the Director of Attendants no longer resided within the Forbidden precinct, and the gentlemen of the Three Bureaus no longer existed; only at outer-palace assemblies did he attend in name.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei and Jin the Director of Attendants no longer dwelt within the Forbidden precinct, and the Three Bureaus of gentlemen were abolished; he attended outer-palace assemblies in name only.

sentences.zh: 二臺奏劾，則符光祿加禁止，解禁止亦如之。

translations.literal: When the Two Bureaus submitted impeachments, a warrant was sent to the Director of Attendants to impose barred entry; lifting barred entry followed the same procedure.
translations.idiomatic: When the Two Bureaus submitted impeachments, a warrant was sent to the Director of Attendants to impose barred entry; lifting the bar followed the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 禁止，身不得入殿省，光祿主殿門故也。

translations.literal: Barred entry meant the person could not enter the palace offices; this was because the Director of Attendants controlled the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Barred entry meant the person could not enter the palace offices, because the Director of Attendants controlled the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 宮殿門戶，至今猶屬。

translations.literal: Palace gates still belong to his charge even today.
translations.idiomatic: Control of the palace gates still belonged to the office even in the present day.

sentences.zh: 晉哀帝興寧二年，省光祿勳，并司徒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xingning under Emperor Ai of Jin, the Director of Attendants was abolished and merged with the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xingning under Emperor Ai of Jin the Director of Attendants was abolished and merged with the Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 孝武寧康元年，復置。

translations.literal: In the first year of Ningkang under Emperor Xiaowu, it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Ningkang under Emperor Xiaowu the office was restored.

sentences.zh: 漢東京三署郎有行應四科者，歲舉茂才二人，四行二人，及三署郎罷省，光祿勳猶依舊舉四行，衣冠子弟充之。

translations.literal: In Later Han's Eastern Capital, gentlemen of the Three Bureaus whose conduct qualified for the Four Categories each year recommended two Outstanding Talents and two men of the Four Virtues; after the Three Bureaus gentlemen were abolished, the Director of Attendants still followed the old practice in recommending men of the Four Virtues, filled by well-born sons of officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han's Eastern Capital, gentlemen of the Three Bureaus whose conduct qualified for the Four Categories each year recommended two Outstanding Talents and two men of the Four Virtues; after the Three Bureaus were abolished the Director of Attendants still followed the old practice of recommending men of the Four Virtues, drawn from well-born sons of officials.

sentences.zh: 三署者，五官署、左署、右署也，各置中郎將以司之。

translations.literal: The Three Bureaus were the Five Officials Bureau, the Left Bureau, and the Right Bureau; each had a Palace Guard General appointed to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Bureaus were the Five Officials Bureau, the Left Bureau, and the Right Bureau, each supervised by a Palace Guard General.

sentences.zh: 郡舉孝廉以補三署郎，年五十以上，屬五官，其次分在左右署。

translations.literal: Commanderies recommended Filial and Incorrupt men to fill the gentlemen of the Three Bureaus; those fifty years of age or above belonged to the Five Officials, and the rest were divided between the Left and Right Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies recommended Filial and Incorrupt men to fill posts in the Three Bureaus; those fifty or older were assigned to the Five Officials Bureau, and the rest were divided between the Left and Right Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 凡有中郎、議郎、侍郎、郎中四等，無員，多至萬人。

translations.literal: In all there were four ranks—Palace Gentleman, Discussion Gentleman, Attendant Gentleman, and Court Gentleman—with no fixed quota, numbering as many as ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: There were four ranks in all—Palace Gentleman, Discussion Gentleman, Attendant Gentleman, and Court Gentleman—with no fixed quota and numbers reaching as high as ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 左光祿大夫，右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Left Director of Attendants Grand Master and Right Director of Attendants Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Left Director of Attendants Grand Master and Right Director of Attendants Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 二大夫，晉初置。

translations.literal: The two grand masters were established at the beginning of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The two grand master posts were established at the founding of Jin.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫，秦時為中大夫，漢武太初元年，更名光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Director of Attendants Grand Master: in Qin times it was Palace Grand Master; in the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu of Han the name was changed to Director of Attendants Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Attendants Grand Master: under Qin it was Palace Grand Master; in the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu of Han it was renamed Director of Attendants Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 晉初又置左右光祿大夫，而光祿大夫如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin the Left and Right Director of Attendants Grand Masters were again established, while the Director of Attendants Grand Master remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Jin the Left and Right Director of Attendants Grandees were added, while the Director of Attendants Grand Master itself remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫銀章青綬，其重者加金章紫綬，則謂之金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The Director of Attendants Grand Master bore a silver seal and blue ribbon; when weightier honors were added with a gold seal and purple ribbon, he was called Grand Master Director of Attendants with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Attendants Grand Master bore a silver seal and blue ribbon; when honored with a gold seal and purple ribbon he was styled Grand Master Director of Attendants with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 舊秩比二千石。

translations.literal: The old rank was stipend equivalent to two thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: The old rank carried a stipend equivalent to two thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 中散大夫，王莽所置，後漢因之，前漢大夫皆無員，掌論議。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Grand Master was established by Wang Mang, and Later Han followed this; in Former Han all grand masters had no fixed quota and oversaw deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Grand Master was established by Wang Mang and retained by Later Han; in Former Han all grand master posts had no fixed quota and handled policy deliberation.

sentences.zh: 後漢光祿大夫三人，中大夫二十人，中散大夫三十人。

translations.literal: Later Han had three Directors of Attendants Grand Master, twenty Palace Grand Masters, and thirty Palace Attendant Grand Masters.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han had three Directors of Attendants Grand Master, twenty Palace Grandees, and thirty Palace Attendant Grandees.

sentences.zh: 魏以來復無員。

translations.literal: Since Wei there was again no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei there was again no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 自左光祿大夫以下，養老疾，無職事。

translations.literal: From the Left Director of Attendants Grand Master downward, they supported the aged and infirm and had no official duties.
translations.idiomatic: From the Left Director of Attendants Grand Master downward, these posts supported the aged and infirm and carried no official duties.

sentences.zh: 中散，六百石。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant, six hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant rank carried a stipend of six hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 衞尉，一人。

translations.literal: Director of the Guard, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Guard: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞二人。

translations.literal: Two assistant directors.
translations.idiomatic: Two assistant directors.

sentences.zh: 掌宮門屯兵，秦官也。

translations.literal: He oversaw palace gate garrison troops; it was a Qin office.
translations.idiomatic: The office oversaw garrison troops at the palace gates; it was a Qin institution.

sentences.zh: 漢景初，改為中大夫令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han Jingdi's reign, it was changed to Director of Palace Grand Masters.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Jing's reign the title was changed to Director of Palace Grandees.

sentences.zh: 後元年，復為衞尉。

translations.literal: In the Houyuan reign year, it was again made Director of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Houyuan reign year it reverted to Director of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 晉江右掌冶鑄，領冶令三十九，戶五千三百五十，冶皆在江北，而江南唯有梅根及冶塘二冶，皆屬揚州，不屬衞尉。

translations.literal: Under Jin on the right bank of the Yangtze it oversaw smelting and casting, administering thirty-nine smeltery directors and five thousand three hundred fifty households; all smelteries were north of the river, while south of the river there were only the Meigang and Yetang smelteries, both subordinate to Yang Province and not to the Director of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin on the right bank of the Yangtze the office oversaw smelting and casting, directing thirty-nine smeltery chiefs and 5,350 households; all smelteries lay north of the river, while south of the river only Meigang and Yetang remained, both under Yang Province rather than the Director of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 衞尉，江左不置，宋世祖孝建元年復置。

translations.literal: Director of the Guard: it was not established east of the Yangtze; in the first year of Xiaojian under Emperor Shizu of Song it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Guard was not retained east of the Yangtze; it was restored in the first year of Xiaojian under Emperor Shizu of Song.

sentences.zh: 舊一丞，世祖增置一丞。

translations.literal: Formerly there was one assistant director; Emperor Shizu added one assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: There had formerly been one assistant director; Emperor Shizu added a second.

sentences.zh: 廷尉，一人。

translations.literal: Commandant of Justice, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Justice: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 掌刑辟。

translations.literal: He oversaw punishments and penal law.
translations.idiomatic: The office oversaw punishments and penal law.

sentences.zh: 凡獄必質之朝廷，與眾共之之義。

translations.literal: In all cases of imprisonment one must submit them to the court for verification—the meaning of sharing judgment with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: All imprisonment cases had to be submitted to the court for verification—the principle of sharing judgment with the multitude.

sentences.zh: 兵獄同制，故曰廷尉。

translations.literal: Military and judicial offices shared the same procedures, hence the name Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Military and judicial matters shared the same procedures, hence the title Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 舜攝帝位，咎繇作士，即其任也。

translations.literal: When Shun acted as regent, Gao Yao served as Minister of Justice—this was the origin of the office.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun served as regent he appointed Gao Yao Minister of Justice; that was the origin of this office.

sentences.zh: 周時大司寇為秋官，掌邦刑。

translations.literal: In Zhou times the Grand Minister of Justice was the Autumn Minister, overseeing the penal law of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou the Grand Minister of Justice was the Autumn Minister charged with the penal law of the realm.

sentences.zh: 秦為廷尉。

translations.literal: Qin made it Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Qin renamed the office Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 漢景帝中六年，更名大理。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the middle Jingdi reign, the name was changed to Grand Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the middle reign of Emperor Jing the office was renamed Grand Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 武帝建元四年，復為廷尉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyuan under Emperor Wu, it was again made Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianyuan under Emperor Wu the title reverted to Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 哀帝元壽二年，復為大理。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanshou under Emperor Ai, it was again made Grand Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanshou under Emperor Ai the office was again renamed Grand Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 漢東京初，復為廷尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Later Han's Eastern Capital, it was again made Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Later Han's Eastern Capital the title reverted to Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 廷尉正，一人。

translations.literal: Commandant of Justice Rectifier, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Justice Rectifier: one post.

sentences.zh: 廷尉監，一人。

translations.literal: Commandant of Justice Supervisor, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Justice Supervisor: one post.

sentences.zh: 正、監並秦官。

translations.literal: The Rectifier and Supervisor were both Qin offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Rectifier and Supervisor were both Qin institutions.

sentences.zh: 本有左右監，漢光武省右，猶云左監；

translations.literal: Originally there were Left and Right Supervisors; Emperor Guangwu of Han eliminated the Right, but it was still called Left Supervisor;
translations.idiomatic: There had originally been Left and Right Supervisors; Emperor Guangwu of Han abolished the Right post but still referred to the Left Supervisor;

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以來，直云監。

translations.literal: Since Wei and Jin, it was simply called Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei and Jin the office was simply called Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 廷尉評，一人。

translations.literal: Commandant of Justice Assessor, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Justice Assessor: one post.

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝地節三年，初置左右評。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dijie under Emperor Xuan of Han, Left and Right Assessors were first established.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dijie under Emperor Xuan of Han the Left and Right Assessors were first established.

sentences.zh: 漢光武省右，猶云左評。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu of Han eliminated the Right, but it was still called Left Assessor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu of Han abolished the Right Assessor but still referred to the Left Assessor.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以來，直云評。

translations.literal: Since Wei and Jin, it was simply called Assessor.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei and Jin the office was simply called Assessor.

sentences.zh: 正、監、評並以下官禮敬廷尉卿。

translations.literal: The Rectifier, Supervisor, and Assessor all paid ritual respect to the Commandant of Justice as subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Rectifier, Supervisor, and Assessor, as subordinate officials, paid ritual respect to the Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 正、監秩千石，評六百石。

translations.literal: The Rectifier and Supervisor ranked at one thousand shi, the Assessor at six hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: The Rectifier and Supervisor carried ranks of one thousand shi, the Assessor six hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 廷尉律博士，一人。

translations.literal: Commandant of Justice Legal Erudite, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Justice Legal Erudite: one post.

sentences.zh: 魏武初建魏國置。

translations.literal: It was established when Cao Wu first founded the state of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The post was established when Cao Cao first founded the state of Wei.

sentences.zh: 大司農，一人。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Revenue, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Revenue: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 掌九穀六畜之供膳羞者。

translations.literal: He oversaw the nine grains and six domestic animals supplied for imperial meals.
translations.idiomatic: The office oversaw supplies of the nine grains and six domestic animals for imperial meals.

sentences.zh: 舜攝帝位，命棄為后稷，即其任也。

translations.literal: When Shun acted as regent, he appointed Qi Minister of Agriculture—this was the origin of the office.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun served as regent he appointed Qi Minister of Agriculture; that was the origin of this office.

sentences.zh: 周則為太府，秦治粟內史，漢景帝後元年，更名大農令，武帝太初元年，更名曰大司農。

translations.literal: Under Zhou it was Grand Treasury; Qin called it Director of Grain Revenue; in the Houyuan year of Emperor Jing of Han the name was changed to Director of Grand Agriculture; in the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu it was again renamed Grand Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou it was the Grand Treasury; Qin called it Director of Grain Revenue; in the Houyuan year of Emperor Jing of Han it became Director of Grand Agriculture; in the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu it was renamed Grand Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 晉哀帝末，省并都水，孝武世復置。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Ai of Jin's reign it was abolished and merged with the Director of Waterways; under Emperor Xiaowu it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Ai of Jin's reign the office was abolished and merged with the Director of Waterways; it was restored under Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 漢世丞二人，魏以來一人。

translations.literal: Under Han there were two assistant directors; since Wei there has been one.
translations.idiomatic: Han had two assistant directors; since Wei there has been only one.

sentences.zh: 太倉令，一人。

translations.literal: Director of the Grand Granary, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Grand Granary: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 秦官也。

translations.literal: It was a Qin office.
translations.idiomatic: This was a Qin institution.

sentences.zh: 晉江左以來，又有東倉、石頭倉丞各一人。

translations.literal: Since Jin east of the Yangtze, there have also been one assistant director each for the Eastern Granary and the Shitou Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jin east of the Yangtze there have also been an assistant director each for the Eastern Granary and the Shitou Granary.

sentences.zh: 䆃官令，一人。

translations.literal: Director of the Winnowing Office, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Winnowing Office: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 掌舂御米。

translations.literal: He oversaw pounding rice for the imperial table.
translations.idiomatic: The office oversaw pounding rice for the imperial table.

sentences.zh: 漢東京置。

translations.literal: It was established in Later Han's Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The office was established in Later Han's Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 䆃，擇也。

translations.literal: Chao means to select.
translations.idiomatic: Chao means to select.

sentences.zh: 擇米令精也。

translations.literal: Selecting rice to make it refined.
translations.idiomatic: It means selecting rice to refine it.

sentences.zh: 司馬相如封禪書云，䆃一莖六穗於庖。

translations.literal: Sima Xiangru's Fengshan Account says, "He winnowed a stalk with six ears in the kitchen."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiangru's Account of the Feng and Shan Sacrifices says, "He winnowed a stalk bearing six ears in the kitchen."

sentences.zh: 籍田令，一人。

translations.literal: Director of the Ceremonial Field, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Ceremonial Field: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 掌耕宗廟社稷之田，於周為甸師。

translations.literal: He oversaw cultivation of the fields for the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain; under Zhou this was the Field Master.
translations.idiomatic: The office oversaw cultivation of the fields for the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain; under Zhou it was the Field Master.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝初立籍田，置令、丞各一人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wen of Han the ceremonial field was established, and one director and one assistant director were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Wen of Han the ceremonial field was established, with one director and one assistant director appointed.

sentences.zh: 漢東京及魏並不置。

translations.literal: Later Han's Eastern Capital and Wei both did not establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Neither Later Han's Eastern Capital nor Wei maintained the office.

sentences.zh: 晉武泰始十年復置。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: It was restored in the tenth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin.

sentences.zh: 江左省。

translations.literal: East of the Yangtze it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Yangtze the office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 宋太祖元嘉中又置。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Taizu of Song in the Yuanjia era it was again established.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizu of Song it was restored again during the Yuanjia era.

sentences.zh: 自太倉至籍田令，並屬司農。

translations.literal: From the Director of the Grand Granary down to the Director of the Ceremonial Field, all were subordinate to the Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: From the Director of the Grand Granary down to the Director of the Ceremonial Field, all were subordinate to the Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 少府，一人。

translations.literal: Minister of the Palace Treasury, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Palace Treasury: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 掌中服御之物。

translations.literal: He oversaw objects for the imperial wardrobe and personal use.
translations.idiomatic: The office oversaw items for the imperial wardrobe and personal use.

sentences.zh: 秦官也，漢因之。

translations.literal: It was a Qin office, and Han followed this.
translations.idiomatic: This was a Qin institution, retained by Han.

sentences.zh: 掌禁錢以給私養，故曰少府。

translations.literal: He oversaw restricted treasury funds to supply the ruler's private expenses, hence the name Minister of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The office controlled restricted treasury funds for the ruler's private expenses, hence the title Minister of the Palace Treasury.

sentences.zh: 晉哀帝末，省并丹陽尹。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Ai of Jin's reign it was abolished and merged with the Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Ai of Jin's reign the office was abolished and merged with the Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 孝武世復置。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowu it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: It was restored under Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 左尚方令、丞各一人。

translations.literal: Left Imperial Workshop Director and assistant director, one each.
translations.idiomatic: Left Imperial Workshop: one director and one assistant director.

sentences.zh: 右尚方令、丞各一人。

translations.literal: Right Imperial Workshop Director and assistant director, one each.
translations.idiomatic: Right Imperial Workshop: one director and one assistant director.

sentences.zh: 並掌造軍器。

translations.literal: Both oversaw the manufacture of military weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Both oversaw the manufacture of military weapons.

sentences.zh: 秦官也，漢因之。

translations.literal: It was a Qin office, and Han followed this.
translations.idiomatic: This was a Qin institution, retained by Han.

sentences.zh: 於周則為玉府。

translations.literal: Under Zhou it was the Jade Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou it was the Jade Treasury.

sentences.zh: 晉江右有中尚方、左尚方、右尚方，江左以來，唯一尚方。

translations.literal: Under Jin on the right bank there were Central, Left, and Right Imperial Workshops; since east of the Yangtze there has been only one Imperial Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin on the right bank there were Central, Left, and Right Imperial Workshops; east of the Yangtze only a single Imperial Workshop has been kept.

sentences.zh: 宋高祖踐阼，以相府作部配臺，謂之左尚方，而本署謂之右尚方焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Song ascended the throne, the workshop department of the chancellor's office was assigned to the central administration and called the Left Imperial Workshop, while the original office was called the Right Imperial Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu of Song took the throne, the workshop department of the chancellor's office was attached to the central administration as the Left Imperial Workshop, while the original office became the Right Imperial Workshop.

sentences.zh: 又以相府細作配臺，即其名置令一人，丞二人，隸門下。

translations.literal: Also the chancellor's fine crafts department was assigned to the central administration; following its name one director and two assistant directors were established, subordinate to the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor's fine-crafts department was also attached to the central administration; a director and two assistant directors were appointed under that name, subordinate to the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 世祖大明中，改曰御府，置令一人，丞一人。

translations.literal: In the Daming era under Emperor Shizu, it was renamed Imperial Wardrobe, with one director and one assistant director established.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daming era under Emperor Shizu it was renamed Imperial Wardrobe, with one director and one assistant director appointed.

sentences.zh: 御府，二漢世典官婢作褻衣服補浣之事，魏、晉猶置其職，江左乃省焉。

translations.literal: The Imperial Wardrobe: in the two Han dynasties it managed palace maid-servants who made undergarments and did mending and washing; Wei and Jin still kept the office, but east of the Yangtze it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Wardrobe: in the two Han dynasties it managed palace maid-servants who made undergarments and handled mending and washing; Wei and Jin retained the office, but east of the Yangtze it was abolished.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝初，省御府，置中署，隸右尚方。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign, the Imperial Wardrobe was abolished and the Central Atelier was established, subordinate to the Right Imperial Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign the Imperial Wardrobe was abolished and a Central Atelier was established under the Right Imperial Workshop.

sentences.zh: 漢東京太僕屬官有考工令，主兵器弓弩刀鎧之屬，成則傳執金吾入武庫，及主織綬諸雜工。

translations.literal: In Later Han's Eastern Capital, among the subordinate officials of the Grand Coachman there was the Director of Works Examination, overseeing weapons, crossbows, blades, armor, and the like; when finished they were transferred through the Bearer of the Gilded Mace into the armory, and he also oversaw weaving of ribbons and various crafts.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han's Eastern Capital the Grand Coachman's staff included a Director of Works Examination who oversaw weapons, crossbows, blades, armor, and the like; finished items were transferred through the Bearer of the Gilded Mace into the armory, and the office also managed weaving of ribbons and various crafts.

sentences.zh: 尚方令唯主作御刀綬劍諸玩好器物而已。

translations.literal: The Imperial Workshop Director only oversaw the making of imperial swords, ribbon seals, blades, and various ornamental objects.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Workshop Director oversaw only the making of imperial swords, ribbon seals, blades, and various ornamental objects.

sentences.zh: 然則考工令如今尚方，尚方令如今中署矣。

translations.literal: Thus the Director of Works Examination corresponds to today's Imperial Workshop, and the Imperial Workshop Director corresponds to today's Central Atelier.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Director of Works Examination corresponds to today's Imperial Workshop, and the Imperial Workshop Director to today's Central Atelier.

sentences.zh: 東冶令，一人。

translations.literal: Director of the Eastern Smeltery, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Eastern Smeltery: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 南冶令，一人。

translations.literal: Director of the Southern Smeltery, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Southern Smeltery: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 漢有鐵官，晉置令，掌工徒鼓鑄，隸衞尉。

translations.literal: Han had an Iron Office; Jin established directors who oversaw craftsmen and laborers in smelting and casting, subordinate to the Director of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Han maintained an Iron Office; Jin appointed directors to oversee craftsmen and laborers in smelting and casting, subordinate to the Director of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，省衞尉，度隸少府。

translations.literal: Since east of the Yangtze the Director of the Guard was abolished, smelteries were transferred to subordination under the Minister of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: After the Director of the Guard was abolished east of the Yangtze, smelteries were transferred to the Minister of the Palace Treasury.

sentences.zh: 宋世雖置衞尉，冶隸少府如故。

translations.literal: Although the Song dynasty restored the Director of the Guard, smelteries remained subordinate to the Minister of the Palace Treasury as before.
translations.idiomatic: Although Song restored the Director of the Guard, smelteries remained under the Minister of the Palace Treasury as before.

sentences.zh: 江南諸郡縣有鐵者或置冶令，或置丞，多是吳所置。

translations.literal: Among commanderies and counties south of the Yangtze where iron was found, some established smeltery directors or assistant directors, mostly set up by Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In commanderies and counties south of the Yangtze where iron was found, some established smeltery directors or assistant directors, mostly set up by Wu.

sentences.zh: 平准令，一人。

translations.literal: Director of Equalization, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Equalization: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 掌染。

translations.literal: He oversaw dyeing.
translations.idiomatic: The office oversaw dyeing.

sentences.zh: 秦官也，漢因之。

translations.literal: It was a Qin office, and Han followed this.
translations.idiomatic: This was a Qin institution, retained by Han.

sentences.zh: 漢隸司農，不知何世隸少府。

translations.literal: Under Han it was subordinate to the Minister of Revenue; at some unknown period it came under the Minister of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han it was subordinate to the Minister of Revenue; at some unknown date it was transferred to the Minister of the Palace Treasury.

sentences.zh: 宋順帝即位，避帝諱，改曰染署。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shun of Song ascended the throne, to avoid the imperial taboo the name was changed to Dyeing Atelier.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shun of Song took the throne the office was renamed Dyeing Atelier to avoid the imperial taboo.

sentences.zh: 將作大匠，一人。

translations.literal: Master of Works, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Works: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 掌土木之役。

translations.literal: He oversaw works of earth and wood.
translations.idiomatic: The office oversaw construction in earth and wood.

sentences.zh: 秦世置將作少府，漢因之。

translations.literal: In Qin times the Minister of Palace Construction Works was established, and Han followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Qin established the Minister of Palace Construction Works, and Han retained the institution.

sentences.zh: 景帝中六年，更名將作大匠。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the Zhong reign era under Emperor Jing, the name was changed to Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Zhong reign era under Emperor Jing, the office was renamed Master of Works.

sentences.zh: 光武建武中元二年省，以謁者領之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu Zhongyuan under Emperor Guangwu it was abolished, and an Usher was put in charge.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu Zhongyuan under Emperor Guangwu the office was abolished, and an Usher took charge of its duties.

sentences.zh: 章帝建初元年復置。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianchu under Emperor Zhang it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianchu under Emperor Zhang the office was restored.

sentences.zh: 晉氏以來，有事則置，無則省。

translations.literal: Since the Jin dynasty, when need arose it was established; when not, it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jin, the office was instituted when needed and abolished when not.

sentences.zh: 大鴻臚，掌贊導拜授諸王。

translations.literal: Grand Herald: he oversaw guiding praise and investing the princes.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Herald oversaw ceremonies of acclaim and the investiture of imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 秦世為典客，漢景帝中六年，更名大行令，武帝太初元年，更名大鴻臚。

translations.literal: In Qin times it was Director of Guests; in the sixth year of Zhong under Emperor Jing of Han it was renamed Grand Master of the Exchanges; in the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu it was renamed Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin the office was Director of Guests; in the sixth year of the Zhong reign era under Emperor Jing of Han it became Grand Master of the Exchanges; in the first year of Taichu under Emperor Wu it was renamed Grand Herald.

sentences.zh: 鴻，大也。

translations.literal: Hong means "great."
translations.idiomatic: Hong means "great."

sentences.zh: 臚，陳也。

translations.literal: Lu means "to set forth" or "to proclaim."
translations.idiomatic: Lu means "to set forth" or "to proclaim."

sentences.zh: 晉江左初省。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin east of the Yangtze it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jin east of the Yangtze the office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 有事則權置，事畢即省。

translations.literal: When need arose it was provisionally established; when the affair was finished it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When need arose it was temporarily instituted and abolished once the business was done.

sentences.zh: 太僕，掌輿馬。

translations.literal: Minister of Transport oversaw chariots and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Transport oversaw chariots and horses.

sentences.zh: 周穆王所置，秦因之。

translations.literal: King Mu of Zhou established it, and Qin followed him.
translations.idiomatic: King Mu of Zhou established the office, and Qin retained it.

sentences.zh: 周官則校人掌馬，巾車掌車，及置太僕，兼其任也。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou the Stable Master oversaw horses and the Chariot Master oversaw chariots; when the Minister of Transport was established, he combined both duties.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Rites of Zhou the Stable Master handled horses and the Chariot Master handled chariots; establishing the Minister of Transport combined both roles.

sentences.zh: 晉江左或置或省，宋以來不置。

translations.literal: Under Jin east of the Yangtze it was sometimes established and sometimes abolished; since Song it has not been established.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin east of the Yangtze the office was sometimes kept and sometimes dropped; since Song it has not been maintained.

sentences.zh: 郊祀則權置太僕執轡，事畢即省。

translations.literal: At suburban sacrifices the Minister of Transport was provisionally established to hold the reins; when finished, it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: For suburban sacrifices a Minister of Transport was temporarily appointed to hold the reins and abolished when the rites were done.

sentences.zh: 太后三卿，各一人。

translations.literal: Three Ministers of the Empress Dowager, one each.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Ministers of the Empress Dowager: one post each.

sentences.zh: 應氏漢官曰：「衞尉、少府，秦官；

translations.literal: Master Ying's Han Offices says: "The Director of the Guard and the Minister of the Palace Treasury were Qin offices;
translations.idiomatic: Master Ying's Han Offices says: "The Director of the Guard and the Minister of the Palace Treasury were Qin offices;

sentences.zh: 太僕，漢成帝置，皆隨太后宮為號，在正卿上，無太后乃闕。」

translations.literal: the Minister of Transport was established by Emperor Cheng of Han—all took their titles from the Empress Dowager's palace, ranked above the regular ministers, and were omitted when there was no empress dowager."
translations.idiomatic: the Minister of Transport was established by Emperor Cheng of Han; all three took their titles from the Empress Dowager's palace, ranked above the regular ministers, and were left unfilled when there was no empress dowager."

sentences.zh: 魏改漢制，在九卿下。

translations.literal: Wei changed the Han system, placing them below the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Wei changed the Han system and placed them below the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 晉復舊，在同號卿上。

translations.literal: Jin restored the old arrangement, ranking them above ministers of the same title.
translations.idiomatic: Jin restored the old arrangement, ranking them above ministers bearing the same title.

sentences.zh: 大長秋，皇后卿也。

translations.literal: Grand Steward of Long Autumn was the empress's minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Steward of Long Autumn was the empress's ministerial office.

sentences.zh: 有后則置，無則省。

translations.literal: When there was an empress it was established; when not, it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The office was kept when there was an empress and dropped when there was not.

sentences.zh: 秦時為將行，漢景帝中六年，更名大長秋。

translations.literal: In Qin times it was Director of Procession; in the sixth year of Zhong under Emperor Jing of Han it was renamed Grand Steward of Long Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin it was Director of Procession; in the sixth year of the Zhong reign era under Emperor Jing of Han it became Grand Steward of Long Autumn.

sentences.zh: 韋曜曰：「長秋者，以皇后陰官，秋者陰之始，取其終而長，欲其久也。」

translations.literal: Wei Yao says: "Long Autumn—because the empress is a yin office; autumn is the beginning of yin; one takes its end and makes it long, wishing her tenure to endure."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yao says: "Long Autumn—because the empress belongs to the yin principle; autumn is where yin begins; the title takes autumn's end and makes it long, wishing her tenure to endure."

sentences.zh: 自太常至長秋，皆置功曹、主簿、五官。

translations.literal: From the Grand Minister of Ceremonies through Long Autumn, all established Merit Officers, Chief Clerks, and Five Officials.
translations.idiomatic: From the Grand Minister of Ceremonies through Long Autumn, each office had Merit Officers, Chief Clerks, and Five Officials.

sentences.zh: 漢東京諸郡有五官掾，因其名也。

translations.literal: In Later Han's Eastern Capital the commanderies had Five-Official Attendants, from which the name derives.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han's Eastern Capital had Five-Official Attendants in the commanderies, from which the title derives.

sentences.zh: 漢制卿尹秩皆中二千石，丞一千石。

translations.literal: Under Han all ministers and directors ranked at middle two thousand bushels, assistants at one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han all ministers and their chiefs ranked at middle two thousand bushels and their assistants at one thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 尚書，古官也。

translations.literal: The Secretariat was an ancient office.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat was an ancient office.

sentences.zh: 舜攝帝位，命龍作納言，即其任也。

translations.literal: When Shun acted as regent, he appointed Dragon as Receiver of Words—that was this office's origin.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun served as regent he appointed Dragon Receiver of Words, which was the origin of this office.

sentences.zh: 周官司會，鄭玄云，若今尚書矣。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou's Director of Accounts—Zheng Xuan says it was like today's Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou's Director of Accounts was, as Zheng Xuan says, comparable to today's Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 秦世少府遣吏四人在殿中主發書，故謂之尚書。

translations.literal: In Qin the Minister of the Palace Treasury sent four clerks to handle outgoing documents in the hall, hence the name Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin the Minister of the Palace Treasury posted four clerks in the hall to dispatch documents, hence the name Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尚猶主也。

translations.literal: Shang means "to preside over."
translations.idiomatic: Shang means "to preside over."

sentences.zh: 漢初有尚冠、尚衣、尚食、尚浴、尚席、尚書，謂之六尚。

translations.literal: Early Han had Director of Caps, Director of Garments, Director of Food, Director of Baths, Director of Mats, and Secretariat—the Six Directors.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han had Directors of Caps, Garments, Food, Baths, and Mats plus the Secretariat, called the Six Directors.

sentences.zh: 戰國時已有尚冠、尚衣之屬矣。

translations.literal: In Warring States times Directors of Caps and Garments and the like already existed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Warring States period Directors of Caps, Garments, and the like already existed.

sentences.zh: 秦時有尚書令、尚書僕射、尚書丞。

translations.literal: Under Qin there were Director of the Secretariat, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Secretariat Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin there were a Director of the Secretariat, a Vice Director of the Secretariat, and an assistant director.

sentences.zh: 至漢初並隸少府，漢東京猶文屬焉。

translations.literal: Down to early Han all were subordinate to the Minister of the Palace Treasury; Later Han's Eastern Capital still nominally attached them to that ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Down to early Han all were subordinate to the Minister of the Palace Treasury; in Later Han's Eastern Capital they remained nominally under that ministry on paper.

sentences.zh: 古者重武官，以善射者掌事，故曰僕射。

translations.literal: In antiquity military offices were valued; skilled archers handled affairs, hence the title Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity military offices were prized; skilled archers handled affairs, hence the title Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 僕射者，僕役於射事也。

translations.literal: Vice Director means one who served in archery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director means one who served in archery affairs.

sentences.zh: 秦世有左右曹諸吏，官無職事，將軍大夫以下皆得加此官。

translations.literal: Under Qin there were Left and Right Bureau clerks—offices without fixed duties; from generals and grand masters downward all could receive this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin there were clerks of the Left and Right Bureaus, offices without fixed duties; anyone from general or grand master rank downward could be given the title.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝世，使左右曹諸吏分平尚書奏事。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu of Han's time, Left and Right Bureau clerks were made to divide and settle Secretariat memorial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Han, clerks of the Left and Right Bureaus were assigned to divide and adjudicate Secretariat memorials.

sentences.zh: 昭帝即位，霍光領尚書事；

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhao ascended, Huo Guang oversaw Secretariat affairs;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhao ascended the throne, Huo Guang oversaw Secretariat affairs;

sentences.zh: 成帝初，王鳳錄尚書事。

translations.literal: at the beginning of Emperor Cheng's reign, Wang Feng recorded Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: at the beginning of Emperor Cheng's reign, Wang Feng served as Recording Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 漢東京每帝即位，輒置太傅，錄尚書事，薨輒省。

translations.literal: In Later Han's Eastern Capital, at each new emperor's accession a Grand Tutor was established to record Secretariat affairs and abolished upon his death.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han's Eastern Capital each new emperor appointed a Grand Tutor as Recording Director of the Secretariat, and the post was abolished when he died.

sentences.zh: 晉康帝世，何充讓錄表曰：「咸康中，分置三錄，王導錄其一，荀崧、陸曄各錄六條事。」

translations.literal: In Emperor Kang of Jin's time, He Chong's memorial declining the Recording Directorship said: "In the Xiankang era three Recording Directors were established; Wang Dao recorded one portion, Xun Song and Lu Ye each recorded six items."
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Kang of Jin, He Chong's memorial declining the Recording Directorship said: "In the Xiankang era three Recording Directors were established; Wang Dao recorded one portion, and Xun Song and Lu Ye each recorded six items."

sentences.zh: 然則似有二十四條，若止有十二條，則荀、陸各錄六條，導又何所司乎？

translations.literal: Then there would seem to be twenty-four items; if there were only twelve, and Xun and Lu each recorded six, what would Dao have overseen?
translations.idiomatic: That would suggest twenty-four items in all; yet if there were only twelve, and Xun and Lu each recorded six, what would Dao have overseen?

sentences.zh: 若導總錄，荀、陸分掌，則不得復云導錄其一也。

translations.literal: If Dao recorded in chief and Xun and Lu divided the management, one could no longer say Dao recorded one portion.
translations.idiomatic: If Dao recorded in chief while Xun and Lu divided the duties, one could no longer say that Dao recorded one portion.

sentences.zh: 其後每置二錄，輒云各掌六條事，又是止有十二條也。

translations.literal: Afterward, whenever two Recording Directors were established, it was always said each managed six items—again suggesting only twelve items.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, whenever two Recording Directors were appointed, it was always said that each managed six items—again implying only twelve items in all.

sentences.zh: 十二條者，不知悉何條。

translations.literal: The twelve items—one does not know fully what they all were.
translations.idiomatic: As for those twelve items, one no longer knows exactly what they were.

sentences.zh: 晉江右有四錄，則四人參錄也。

translations.literal: Under Jin west of the Yangtze there were four Recording Directors, so four men shared the recording duties.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin on the right bank there were four Recording Directors, so four men jointly held the recording role.

sentences.zh: 江右張華、江左庾亮並經關尚書七條，則亦不知皆何事也。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua on the right bank and Yu Liang on the left both once oversaw seven Secretariat items—again one does not know what they all were.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua west of the Yangtze and Yu Liang east of it both once supervised seven Secretariat items, and those too are now unknown.

sentences.zh: 後何充解錄，又參關尚書。

translations.literal: Later when He Chong resigned the Recording Directorship, he again shared oversight of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after He Chong resigned the Recording Directorship, he again shared oversight of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 錄尚書職無不總，王肅注尚書「納于大麓」曰：「堯納舜於尊顯之官，使大錄萬機之政也。」

translations.literal: The Recording Director's duties embraced everything; Wang Su's commentary on the Book of Documents passage "received him on Mount Lu" says: "Yao received Shun in an exalted office, making him broadly record the myriad affairs of state."
translations.idiomatic: The Recording Director's duties embraced everything; Wang Su's commentary on the Book of Documents passage "received him on Mount Lu" says: "Yao received Shun in an exalted office and made him broadly record the myriad affairs of state."

sentences.zh: 凡重號將軍刺史，皆得命曹授用，唯不得施除及加節。

translations.literal: All generals of weighty rank and inspectors could have their staff appointed and employed through the bureaus, but could not grant appointments and dismissals or confer seals of authority.
translations.idiomatic: All generals of weighty rank and inspectors could have their staff appointed and employed through the bureaus, but could not grant appointments and dismissals or confer seals of authority.

sentences.zh: 宋世祖孝建中，不欲威權外假，省錄。

translations.literal: In the Xiaojian era under Emperor Shizu of Song, not wishing to lend authority and power abroad, the Recording Directorship was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaojian era under Emperor Shizu of Song the court, unwilling to delegate supreme authority outward, abolished the Recording Directorship.

sentences.zh: 大明末復置。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daming era it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daming era it was restored.

sentences.zh: 此後或置或省。

translations.literal: After that it was sometimes established and sometimes abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the office was sometimes kept and sometimes dropped.

sentences.zh: 漢獻帝建安四年，以執金吾榮郃為尚書左僕射，衞臻為右僕射。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jian'an under Emperor Xian of Han, Commandant of the Capital Rong He was made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Wei Zhen Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jian'an under Emperor Xian of Han, Commandant of the Capital Rong He became Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Wei Zhen Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 二僕射分置，自此始也。

translations.literal: The separate establishment of two Vice Directors began here.
translations.idiomatic: The separate appointment of two Vice Directors began at this point.

sentences.zh: 漢成帝建始四年，初置尚書，員四人，增丞亦為四人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianshi under Emperor Cheng of Han, Secretaries were first established at four posts, and assistant directors were also increased to four.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianshi under Emperor Cheng of Han four Secretariat ministers were first established, with assistant directors also increased to four.

sentences.zh: 曹尚書其一曰常侍曹，主公卿事；

translations.literal: Of the Secretariat bureaus, the first was the Attendant Service Bureau, overseeing grand masters and ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Of the Secretariat bureaus, the first was the Attendant Service Bureau, which handled affairs of grandees and ministers;

sentences.zh: 其二曰二千石曹，主郡國二千石事；

translations.literal: the second was the Two-Thousand-Bushel Bureau, overseeing commandery and state two-thousand-bushel officials;
translations.idiomatic: the second was the Two-Thousand-Bushel Bureau, which handled commandery and state officials of two thousand bushels;

sentences.zh: 其三曰民曹，主吏民上書事；

translations.literal: the third was the People Bureau, overseeing commoners' and officials' memorials;
translations.idiomatic: the third was the People Bureau, which handled memorials from officials and commoners;

sentences.zh: 其四曰客曹，主外國夷狄事。

translations.literal: the fourth was the Guest Bureau, overseeing foreign states and barbarian peoples.
translations.idiomatic: the fourth was the Guest Bureau, which handled foreign states and frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 光武分二千石曹為二，又分客曹為南主客曹、北主客曹，改常侍曹為吏曹，凡六尚書。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu divided the Two-Thousand-Bushel Bureau in two, also divided the Guest Bureau into Southern and Northern Guest Bureaus, changed Attendant Service to the Personnel Bureau—six Secretaries in all.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu split the Two-Thousand-Bushel Bureau in two, divided the Guest Bureau into Southern and Northern Guest Bureaus, and renamed Attendant Service the Personnel Bureau, for six Secretariat ministers in all.

sentences.zh: 減二丞，唯置左右二丞而已。

translations.literal: Two assistant directors were cut; only left and right assistant directors were kept.
translations.idiomatic: Two assistant director posts were cut, leaving only left and right assistant directors.

sentences.zh: 應劭漢官云：「尚書令、左丞，總領綱紀，無所不統。

translations.literal: Ying Shao's Han Offices says: "The Director of the Secretariat and Left Assistant Director overall commanded the regulations, overseeing all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao's Han Offices says: "The Director of the Secretariat and the Left Assistant Director commanded the regulations overall and oversaw all affairs.

sentences.zh: 僕射、右丞，掌稟假錢穀。

translations.literal: The Vice Director and Right Assistant Director handled grants and loans of money and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Director and Right Assistant Director handled grants and loans of money and grain.

sentences.zh: 三公尚書二人，掌天下歲盡集課；

translations.literal: Two Three-Dukes Secretaries handled annual nationwide performance assessments;
translations.idiomatic: Two Three-Dukes Secretaries handled annual nationwide performance assessments;

sentences.zh: 吏曹掌選舉、齋祠；

translations.literal: the Personnel Bureau handled selection and appointment and fasting sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: the Personnel Bureau handled selection and appointment and fasting sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 二千石曹掌水、火、盜賊、詞訟、罪法；

translations.literal: the Two-Thousand-Bushel Bureau handled flood, fire, theft, litigation, and criminal law;
translations.idiomatic: the Two-Thousand-Bushel Bureau handled flood, fire, theft, litigation, and criminal law;

sentences.zh: 客曹掌羌、胡朝會，法駕出，護駕；

translations.literal: the Guest Bureau handled Qiang and Hu audiences, imperial processions, and escort of the imperial carriage;
translations.idiomatic: the Guest Bureau handled Qiang and Hu audiences, imperial processions, and escort of the imperial carriage;

sentences.zh: 民曹掌繕治、功作、鹽池、苑囿。

translations.literal: the People Bureau handled repairs, public works, salt ponds, and imperial parks.
translations.idiomatic: the People Bureau handled repairs, public works, salt ponds, and imperial parks.

sentences.zh: 吏曹任要，多得超遷。」

translations.literal: The Personnel Bureau held crucial duties, and many were promoted beyond ordinary rank."
translations.idiomatic: The Personnel Bureau held crucial duties, and many of its incumbents received exceptional promotion."

sentences.zh: 則漢末曹名及職司又與光武時異也。

translations.literal: Thus the bureau names and duties at the end of Han again differed from Emperor Guangwu's time.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the bureau names and duties at the end of Han again differed from Emperor Guangwu's time.

sentences.zh: 魏世有吏部、左民、客曹、五兵、度支五曹尚書。

translations.literal: Under Wei there were five Bureau Secretaries: Personnel, Left People, Guest, Five Armies, and Revenue Disbursement.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei there were five Bureau Secretaries: Personnel, Left People, Guest Affairs, Five Armies, and Revenue Disbursement.

sentences.zh: 晉初有吏部、三公、客曹、駕部、屯田、度支六曹尚書。

translations.literal: Early Jin had six Bureau Secretaries: Personnel, Three Dukes, Guest, Chariot, Colony Fields, and Revenue Disbursement.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jin had six Bureau Secretaries: Personnel, Three Dukes, Guest Affairs, Chariot, Colony Fields, and Revenue Disbursement.

sentences.zh: 武帝咸寧二年，省駕部尚書，四年又置。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianning under Emperor Wu the Chariot Secretary was abolished; in the fourth year it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianning under Emperor Wu the Chariot Secretary was abolished and restored in the fourth year.

sentences.zh: 太康中，有吏部、殿中、五兵、田曹、度支、左民六尚書。

translations.literal: In the Taikang era there were six Secretaries: Personnel, Palace, Five Armies, Field, Revenue Disbursement, and Left People.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taikang era there were six Secretariat ministers: Personnel, Palace, Five Armies, Field, Revenue Disbursement, and Left People.

sentences.zh: 惠帝世，又有右民尚書。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Hui there was also a Right People Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui a Right People Secretary was also added.

sentences.zh: 尚書止於六曹，不知此時省何曹也。

translations.literal: Secretaries were limited to six bureaus; one does not know which bureau was abolished at this time.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat was limited to six bureaus, but which bureau was dropped at this point is unknown.

sentences.zh: 江左則有祠部、吏部、左民、度支、五兵，合為五曹尚書。

translations.literal: East of the Yangtze there were Sacrificial, Personnel, Left People, Revenue Disbursement, and Five Armies—five Bureau Secretaries in all.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Yangtze there were Sacrificial, Personnel, Left People, Revenue Disbursement, and Five Armies Bureaus, five Secretariat ministers in all.

sentences.zh: 宋高祖初，又增都官尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu of Song, a Capital Crimes Secretary was added.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Song, Emperor Gaozu added a Capital Crimes Secretary.

sentences.zh: 若有右僕射，則不置祠部尚書。

translations.literal: If there was a Right Vice Director, the Sacrificial Secretary was not established.
translations.idiomatic: When a Right Vice Director was in place, no Sacrificial Secretary was appointed.

sentences.zh: 世祖大明二年，置二吏部尚書，而省五兵尚書，後還置一吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming under Emperor Shizu, two Personnel Secretaries were established while the Five Armies Secretary was abolished; later one Personnel Secretary was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming under Emperor Shizu two Personnel Secretaries were appointed and the Five Armies Secretary dropped; later a single Personnel Secretary was restored.

sentences.zh: 順帝昇明元年，又置五兵尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengming under Emperor Shun, the Five Armies Secretary was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shengming under Emperor Shun the Five Armies Secretary was restored.

sentences.zh: 尚書令，任總機衡；

translations.literal: The Director of the Secretariat held overall charge of the pivot of state;
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Secretariat held overall charge of the pivot of state;

sentences.zh: 僕射、尚書，分領諸曹。

translations.literal: Vice Directors and Secretaries divided oversight of the bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Directors and bureau Secretaries divided oversight of the bureaus.

sentences.zh: 左僕射領殿中、主客二曹；

translations.literal: The Left Vice Director oversaw the Palace and Guest bureaus;
translations.idiomatic: The Left Vice Director oversaw the Palace and Guest bureaus;

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書領吏部、刪定、三公、比部四曹；

translations.literal: the Personnel Secretary oversaw Personnel, Revisions, Three Dukes, and Comparison bureaus;
translations.idiomatic: the Personnel Secretary oversaw the Personnel, Revisions, Three Dukes, and Comparison bureaus;

sentences.zh: 祠部尚書領祠部、儀曹二曹；

translations.literal: the Sacrificial Secretary oversaw Sacrificial and Ritual bureaus;
translations.idiomatic: the Sacrificial Secretary oversaw the Sacrificial and Ritual bureaus;

sentences.zh: 度支尚書領度支、金部、倉部、起部四曹；

translations.literal: the Revenue Disbursement Secretary oversaw Revenue Disbursement, Mint, Granary, and Construction bureaus;
translations.idiomatic: the Revenue Disbursement Secretary oversaw the Revenue Disbursement, Mint, Granary, and Construction bureaus;

sentences.zh: 左民尚書領左民、駕部二曹；

translations.literal: the Left People Secretary oversaw Left People and Chariot bureaus;
translations.idiomatic: the Left People Secretary oversaw the Left People and Chariot bureaus;

sentences.zh: 都官尚書領都官、水部、庫部、功論四曹；

translations.literal: the Capital Crimes Secretary oversaw Capital Crimes, Waterways, Storehouse, and Works Review bureaus;
translations.idiomatic: the Capital Crimes Secretary oversaw the Capital Crimes, Waterways, Storehouse, and Works Review bureaus;

sentences.zh: 五兵尚書領中兵、外兵二曹。

translations.literal: the Five Armies Secretary oversaw Central and External Military bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: the Five Armies Secretary oversaw the Central and External Military bureaus.

sentences.zh: 昔有騎兵、別兵、都兵，故謂之五兵也。

translations.literal: Formerly there were Cavalry, Separate, and Capital Armies bureaus, hence the name Five Armies.
translations.idiomatic: There had once been Cavalry, Separate, and Capital Armies bureaus, which is why the office was called Five Armies.

sentences.zh: 五尚書、二僕射、一令，謂之八坐。

translations.literal: Five Secretaries, two Vice Directors, and one Director were called the Eight Dignitaries.
translations.idiomatic: Five bureau Secretaries, two Vice Directors, and one Director made up the Eight Dignitaries.

sentences.zh: 若營宗廟宮室，則置起部尚書，事畢省。

translations.literal: When constructing ancestral temples or palaces, a Construction Secretary was established and abolished when finished.
translations.idiomatic: When ancestral temples or palaces were under construction, a Construction Secretary was appointed and abolished once the work was done.

sentences.zh: 漢成帝之置四尚書也，無置郎之文。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng of Han established four Secretaries, there is no text establishing Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Cheng of Han established four Secretariat ministers, no source also establishes Attendants.

sentences.zh: 漢儀，尚書郎四人，一人主匈奴單于營部，一人主羌夷吏民，一人主戶口墾田，一人主財帛委輸。

translations.literal: Han Protocol: four Secretariat Attendants—one oversaw the Xiongnu chanyu's encampment district, one Qiang and barbarian officials and people, one household registers and reclaimed fields, one treasury goods and transport.
translations.idiomatic: Han Protocol records four Secretariat Attendants: one for the Xiongnu chanyu's encampment district, one for Qiang and other frontier peoples, one for population registers and reclaimed land, and one for treasury goods and transport.

sentences.zh: 匈奴單于，宣帝之世，保塞內附，成帝世，單于還北庭矣。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu chanyu: in Emperor Xuan's time he came within the frontier to submit; in Emperor Cheng's time the chanyu returned to the Northern Court.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Xiongnu chanyu, under Emperor Xuan he submitted and settled within the frontier; under Emperor Cheng the chanyu returned to the Northern Court.

sentences.zh: 一郎主匈奴單于營部，則置郎疑是光武時，所主匈奴，是南單于也。

translations.literal: One Attendant oversaw the Xiongnu chanyu's encampment district; as for when Attendants were established, this was probably in Guangwu's time; the Xiongnu he oversaw was the Southern Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: One Attendant was charged with the Xiongnu chanyu's encampment district; the post probably dates to Guangwu's reign, when the Xiongnu in question was the Southern Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 漢官云，置郎三十六人，不知是何帝增員。

translations.literal: Han Official Records says thirty-six Attendants were established; it is not known under which emperor the roster was expanded.
translations.idiomatic: Han Official Records records thirty-six Attendants on the roster, but it is unclear which emperor added to their number.

sentences.zh: 然則一尚書則領六郎也。

translations.literal: Thus one Secretary oversaw six Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Thus each Secretariat minister oversaw six Attendants.

sentences.zh: 主作文書，起立事草。

translations.literal: They oversaw drafting documents and standing memorial drafts.
translations.idiomatic: They drafted documents and prepared memorial drafts for court business.

sentences.zh: 初為郎中，滿歲則為侍郎。

translations.literal: At first one served as Court Gentleman; after a full year one became Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: One began as a Court Gentleman and, after a full year, was promoted to Attendant.

sentences.zh: 尚書寺居建禮門內。

translations.literal: The Secretariat office was located inside the Jianli Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat office stood inside the Jianli Gate.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎入直，官供青縑白綾被，或以綿緤為之。

translations.literal: When Secretariat Attendants entered duty, the office supplied green silk and white damask quilts, or sometimes made them of padded cotton cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When Secretariat Attendants went on duty, the office furnished green silk and white damask quilts, sometimes padded with cotton cloth instead.

sentences.zh: 給帷帳、氈褥、通中枕，太官供食物，湯官供餅餌及五孰果實之屬，給尚書伯使一人，女侍二人，皆選端正妖麗，執香爐，護衣服，奏事明光殿。
