translations.literal: They were supplied with curtains, felt mattresses, and hollow-center pillows; the Grand Provisioner supplied food, the Hot-Water Office supplied cakes and the five kinds of cooked fruits, and one Secretariat usher and two female attendants were assigned—all chosen for fine looks and beauty—to carry incense burners, tend garments, and present memorials in the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: They received curtains, felt bedding, and hollow-center pillows; the Grand Provisioner supplied meals, the Hot-Water Office supplied cakes and five kinds of cooked fruit, and one Secretariat usher plus two female attendants were assigned—all chosen for striking beauty—to carry incense burners, tend clothing, and present memorials in the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 殿以胡粉塗壁，畫古賢烈士。

translations.literal: The hall's walls were coated with whitewash and painted with ancient worthies and martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: The hall walls were whitewashed and painted with ancient worthies and martyrs.

sentences.zh: 以丹朱色地，謂之丹墀。

translations.literal: The ground was cinnabar red and was called the cinnabar courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The floor was cinnabar red and was called the cinnabar courtyard.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎口含雞舌香，以其奏事答對，欲使氣息芬芳也。

translations.literal: Secretariat Attendants held cloves in their mouths when presenting memorials and answering, so that their breath would be fragrant.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Attendants kept cloves in their mouths when presenting memorials and answering questions, so their breath would stay fragrant.

sentences.zh: 奏事則與黃門侍郎對揖。

translations.literal: When presenting memorials they bowed facing the Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When presenting memorials they exchanged bows with the Yellow Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎稱已聞，乃出。

translations.literal: The Yellow Gate Attendant would say he had heard, and then they would leave.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Yellow Gate Attendant said he had heard, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 天子所服五時衣以賜尚書令僕，而丞、郎月賜赤管大筆一雙，隃麋墨一丸。

translations.literal: The five seasonal garments worn by the Son of Heaven were granted to the Secretariat Director and Vice Directors, while Assistant Directors and Attendants monthly received one pair of red-shafted large brushes and one cake of Youmi ink.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven's five seasonal garments were granted to the Secretariat Director and Vice Directors, while Assistant Directors and Attendants each month received one pair of red-shafted large brushes and one cake of Youmi ink.

sentences.zh: 魏世有殿中、吏部、駕部、金部、虞曹、比部、南主客、祠部、度支、庫部、農部、水部、儀曹、三公、倉部、民曹、二千石、中兵、外兵、別兵、都兵、考功、定科，凡二十三郎。

translations.literal: Under Wei there were Palace Affairs, Personnel, Chariot, Mint, Parks, Comparisons, Southern Foreign Affairs, Sacrificial, Revenue Disbursement, Storehouse, Agriculture, Waterways, Ritual, Three Ducal Offices, Granary, People, Two-Thousand-shi, Central Military, External Military, Separate Military, Capital Armies, Merit Assessment, and Statutory Codes Attendants—in all twenty-three bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei there were twenty-three bureau Attendants: Palace Affairs, Personnel, Chariot, Mint, Parks, Comparisons, Southern Foreign Affairs, Sacrificial, Revenue Disbursement, Storehouse, Agriculture, Waterways, Ritual, Three Ducal Offices, Granary, People, Two-Thousand-shi, Central Military, External Military, Separate Military, Capital Armies, Merit Assessment, and Statutory Codes.

sentences.zh: 青龍二年有軍事，尚書令陳矯奏置都官、騎兵二曹郎，合為二十五曹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qinglong, because of military affairs, Secretariat Director Chen Qiao memorialized to establish Capital Crimes and Cavalry bureau Attendants, making twenty-five bureaus in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qinglong, amid military operations, Secretariat Director Chen Qiao memorialized to add Capital Crimes and Cavalry bureau Attendants, bringing the total to twenty-five bureaus.

sentences.zh: 晉西朝則直事、殿中、祠部、儀曹、吏部、三公、比部、金部、倉部、度支、都官、二千石、左民、右民、虞曹、屯田、起部、水部、左主客、右主客、駕部、車部、庫部、左中兵、右中兵、左外兵、右外兵、別兵、都兵、騎兵、左士、右士、北主客、南主客為三十四曹郎；

translations.literal: Under the Western Jin court there were Direct Affairs, Palace Affairs, Sacrificial, Ritual, Personnel, Three Ducal Offices, Comparisons, Mint, Granary, Revenue Disbursement, Capital Crimes, Two-Thousand-shi, Left People, Right People, Parks, Garrison Agriculture, Construction, Waterways, Left Foreign Affairs, Right Foreign Affairs, Chariot, Cart, Storehouse, Left Central Military, Right Central Military, Left External Military, Right External Military, Separate Military, Capital Armies, Cavalry, Left Scholar, Right Scholar, Northern Foreign Affairs, and Southern Foreign Affairs Attendants—thirty-four bureaus in all;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Western Jin court there were thirty-four bureau Attendants: Direct Affairs, Palace Affairs, Sacrificial, Ritual, Personnel, Three Ducal Offices, Comparisons, Mint, Granary, Revenue Disbursement, Capital Crimes, Two-Thousand-shi, Left People, Right People, Parks, Garrison Agriculture, Construction, Waterways, Left Foreign Affairs, Right Foreign Affairs, Chariot, Cart, Storehouse, Left Central Military, Right Central Military, Left External Military, Right External Military, Separate Military, Capital Armies, Cavalry, Left Scholar, Right Scholar, Northern Foreign Affairs, and Southern Foreign Affairs;

sentences.zh: 後又置運曹，凡三十五曹。

translations.literal: Later Transport bureau was also established, making thirty-five bureaus in all.
translations.idiomatic: Transport bureau was added later, for thirty-five bureaus in all.

sentences.zh: 晉江左初，無直事、右民、屯田、車部、別兵、都兵、騎兵、左士、右士、運曹十曹郎，而主客、中外兵各置一郎而已，所餘十七曹也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Eastern Jin south of the Yangtze there were no Direct Affairs, Right People, Garrison Agriculture, Cart, Separate Military, Capital Armies, Cavalry, Left Scholar, Right Scholar, or Transport bureau Attendants—only one Attendant each for Foreign Affairs and for Central and External Military, leaving seventeen bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Eastern Jin south of the Yangtze, ten bureaus were absent: Direct Affairs, Right People, Garrison Agriculture, Cart, Separate Military, Capital Armies, Cavalry, Left Scholar, Right Scholar, and Transport; Foreign Affairs and Central and External Military each had only one Attendant, leaving seventeen bureaus.

sentences.zh: 康、穆以來，又無虞曹、二千石二郎，猶有殿中、祠部、吏部、儀曹、三公、比部、金部、倉部、度支、都官、左民、起部、水部、主客、駕部、庫部、中兵、外兵十八曹郎。

translations.literal: Since the Kang and Mu reigns, Parks and Two-Thousand-shi bureaus were also absent, but there remained Palace Affairs, Sacrificial, Personnel, Ritual, Three Ducal Offices, Comparisons, Mint, Granary, Revenue Disbursement, Capital Crimes, Left People, Construction, Waterways, Foreign Affairs, Chariot, Storehouse, Central Military, and External Military Attendants—eighteen bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: From the Kang and Mu reigns onward, Parks and Two-Thousand-shi bureaus were also dropped, but eighteen bureaus remained: Palace Affairs, Sacrificial, Personnel, Ritual, Three Ducal Offices, Comparisons, Mint, Granary, Revenue Disbursement, Capital Crimes, Left People, Construction, Waterways, Foreign Affairs, Chariot, Storehouse, Central Military, and External Military.

sentences.zh: 後又省主客、起部、水部，餘十五曹。

translations.literal: Later Foreign Affairs, Construction, and Waterways bureaus were also abolished, leaving fifteen bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign Affairs, Construction, and Waterways bureaus were later abolished as well, leaving fifteen bureaus.

sentences.zh: 宋高祖初，加置騎兵、主客、起部、水部四曹郎，合為十九曹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu of Song, Cavalry, Foreign Affairs, Construction, and Waterways bureau Attendants were added, making nineteen bureaus in all.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Gaozu of Song's reign, Cavalry, Foreign Affairs, Construction, and Waterways bureau Attendants were restored, for nineteen bureaus in all.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉十年，又省儀曹、主客、比部、騎部四曹郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Taizu, Ritual, Foreign Affairs, Comparisons, and Cavalry bureau Attendants were again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Taizu, Ritual, Foreign Affairs, Comparisons, and Cavalry bureau Attendants were abolished again.

sentences.zh: 十一年，又並置。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, all were restored together.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year all four were restored together.

sentences.zh: 十八年，增刪定曹郎，次在左民曹上，蓋魏世之定科郎也。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Editorial Revision bureau Attendant was added, ranking above Left People bureau—probably Wei's Statutory Codes Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year an Editorial Revision bureau Attendant was added, ranking above Left People bureau—likely the successor to Wei's Statutory Codes Attendant.

sentences.zh: 三十年，又置功論郎，次都官之下，在刪定之上。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, Works Review Attendant was also established, ranking below Capital Crimes and above Editorial Revision.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year a Works Review Attendant was also added, ranking below Capital Crimes and above Editorial Revision.

sentences.zh: 太宗世，省騎兵。

translations.literal: In Emperor Taizong's time, Cavalry bureau was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong, the Cavalry bureau was abolished.

sentences.zh: 今凡二十曹郎。

translations.literal: At present there are twenty bureau Attendants in all.
translations.idiomatic: At present there are twenty bureau Attendants in all.

sentences.zh: 以三公、比部主法制。

translations.literal: The Three Ducal Offices and Comparisons bureaus oversaw legal institutions.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Ducal Offices and Comparisons bureaus oversaw legal institutions.

sentences.zh: 度支主算。

translations.literal: Revenue Disbursement oversaw accounting.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue Disbursement oversaw accounting.

sentences.zh: 支，派也。

translations.literal: Zhi means branch or faction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi means branch or faction.

sentences.zh: 度，景也。

translations.literal: Du means measure or extent.
translations.idiomatic: Du means measure or extent.

sentences.zh: 都官主軍事刑獄。

translations.literal: Capital Crimes oversaw military affairs and prisons.
translations.idiomatic: Capital Crimes oversaw military affairs and prisons.

sentences.zh: 其餘曹所掌，各如其名。

translations.literal: The remaining bureaus' responsibilities each matched their names.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining bureaus handled duties that matched their names.

sentences.zh: 漢制，公卿御史中丞以下，遇尚書令、僕、丞、郎，皆辟車豫相回避，臺官過，乃得去。

translations.literal: Under Han regulation, from the Three Ducal Ministers and Imperial Secretary down, when encountering the Secretariat Director, Vice Directors, Assistant Directors, and Attendants, all would stop their carriages and move aside to yield; only after the Secretariat officials passed could they proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han regulation, from the Three Ducal Ministers and Imperial Secretary downward, anyone meeting the Secretariat Director, Vice Directors, Assistant Directors, or Attendants had to stop the carriage and pull aside to yield; only after the Secretariat officials had passed could they move on.

sentences.zh: 今尚書官上朝及下，禁斷行人，猶其制也。

translations.literal: Today when Secretariat officials go to or leave court, pedestrian traffic is blocked—still the same regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Today, when Secretariat officials go to or leave court, pedestrian traffic is still blocked—the same regulation.

sentences.zh: 漢又制，丞、郎見尚書，呼曰明時。

translations.literal: Han also regulated that when Assistant Directors and Attendants saw a Secretary, they called out Ming shi.
translations.idiomatic: Han custom also required that when Assistant Directors and Attendants encountered a Secretary, they called out Ming shi.

sentences.zh: 郎見二丞。

translations.literal: When Attendants saw the two Assistant Directors,
translations.idiomatic: When Attendants encountered the two Assistant Directors,

sentences.zh: 呼曰左君、右君。

translations.literal: they called out Lord Left and Lord Right.
translations.idiomatic: they called out Lord Left and Lord Right.

sentences.zh: 郎以下則有都令史、令史、書令史、書吏幹。

translations.literal: Below Attendants were Chief Clerks, Clerks, Document Clerks, and Document Assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Below the Attendants were Chief Clerks, Clerks, Document Clerks, and Document Assistants.

sentences.zh: 漢東京尚書令史十八人，晉初正令史百二十人，書令史百三十人。

translations.literal: Eastern Capital Han had eighteen Secretariat Clerks; early Jin had one hundred twenty regular Clerks and one hundred thirty Document Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Capital Han had eighteen Secretariat Clerks; early Jin had 120 regular Clerks and 130 Document Clerks.

sentences.zh: 自晉至今，或減或益，難以定言。

translations.literal: From Jin to the present, numbers have increased or decreased—it is hard to state definitively.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin to the present the numbers have fluctuated, so no fixed figure can be given.

sentences.zh: 漢儀有丞相令史。

translations.literal: Han Protocol records Chancellor Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Han Protocol records Chancellor Clerks.

sentences.zh: 令史蓋前漢官也。

translations.literal: Clerks were probably an office of Former Han.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks were probably an institution of Former Han.

sentences.zh: 晉西朝有尚書都令史朱誕，則都令史其來久矣。

translations.literal: The Western Jin court had Secretariat Chief Clerk Zhu Yan, so Chief Clerks date back far.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Jin court had a Secretariat Chief Clerk named Zhu Yan, so Chief Clerks must date back much earlier.

sentences.zh: 分曹所掌如尚書也。

translations.literal: Each bureau's responsibilities matched those of the Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Each bureau's duties matched those of the corresponding Secretariat ministers.

sentences.zh: 晉西朝八坐丞郎，朝晡詣都坐朝，江左唯旦朝而已。

translations.literal: Under the Western Jin court the Eight Dignitaries, Assistant Directors, and Attendants attended morning and evening sessions at the collective seating hall; east of the Yangtze there were only morning sessions.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Western Jin court the Eight Dignitaries, Assistant Directors, and Attendants attended morning and evening sessions at the collective seating hall; east of the Yangtze only the morning session remained.

sentences.zh: 八坐丞郎初拜，並集都坐，交禮。

translations.literal: When the Eight Dignitaries, Assistant Directors, and Attendants were first appointed, all gathered at the collective seating hall to exchange courtesies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eight Dignitaries, Assistant Directors, and Attendants were first appointed, all gathered at the collective seating hall to exchange courtesies.

sentences.zh: 遷，又解交。

translations.literal: On transfer, they exchanged farewell courtesies.
translations.idiomatic: On transfer they exchanged farewell courtesies.

sentences.zh: 漢舊制也。

translations.literal: This was Former Han custom.
translations.idiomatic: This was Former Han custom.

sentences.zh: 今唯八坐解交，丞郎不復解交也。

translations.literal: Now only the Eight Dignitaries exchange farewell courtesies; Assistant Directors and Attendants no longer do.
translations.idiomatic: Now only the Eight Dignitaries exchange farewell courtesies; Assistant Directors and Attendants no longer do.

sentences.zh: 尚書令千石，僕射尚書六百石，丞郎四百石。

translations.literal: The Secretariat Director ranked at one thousand shi, the Vice Director of the Secretariat at six hundred shi, and Assistant Directors and Attendants at four hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat Director ranked at one thousand shi, the Vice Director at six hundred shi, and Assistant Directors and Attendants at four hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 武庫令，一人。

translations.literal: Arsenal Director, one post.
translations.idiomatic: Arsenal Director: one post.

sentences.zh: 掌軍器。

translations.literal: He oversaw military equipment.
translations.idiomatic: The office oversaw military equipment.

sentences.zh: 秦官。

translations.literal: Qin office.
translations.idiomatic: It was a Qin institution.

sentences.zh: 至二漢，屬執金吾。

translations.literal: Through both Han dynasties it was subordinate to the Commandant of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Through both Han dynasties it was subordinate to the Commandant of the Capital.

sentences.zh: 晉初罷執金吾，至今隸尚書庫部。

translations.literal: Early Jin abolished the Commandant of the Capital; to the present it has been subordinate to the Secretariat Storehouse bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jin abolished the Commandant of the Capital, and since then the office has been subordinate to the Secretariat Storehouse bureau.

sentences.zh: 車府令，一人。

translations.literal: Chariot Office Director, one post.
translations.idiomatic: Chariot Office Director: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 秦官也。

translations.literal: It was a Qin office.
translations.idiomatic: It was a Qin institution.

sentences.zh: 二漢、魏、晉並隸太僕。

translations.literal: Under both Han, Wei, and Jin it was subordinate to the Grand Master of the Household for Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Under both Han, Wei, and Jin it was subordinate to the Grand Master of the Household for Chariots.

sentences.zh: 太僕既省，隸尚書駕部。

translations.literal: After the Grand Master of the Household for Chariots was abolished, it was subordinate to the Secretariat Chariot bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After the Grand Master of the Household for Chariots was abolished, the office was placed under the Secretariat Chariot bureau.

sentences.zh: 上林令，一人。

translations.literal: Shanglin Park Director, one post.
translations.idiomatic: Shanglin Park Director: one post.

sentences.zh: 丞一人。

translations.literal: One assistant director.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director.

sentences.zh: 漢西京上林中有八丞、十二尉、十池監。

translations.literal: Western Capital Han Shanglin Park had eight assistant directors, twelve commandants, and ten pond supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: Western Capital Han's Shanglin Park had eight assistant directors, twelve commandants, and ten pond supervisors.

sentences.zh: 丞、尉屬水衡都尉。

translations.literal: The assistant directors and commandants were subordinate to the Director of Waterways and Forestry.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant directors and commandants were subordinate to the Director of Waterways and Forestry.

sentences.zh: 池監隸少府。

translations.literal: The pond supervisors were subordinate to the Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: The pond supervisors were subordinate to the Privy Treasurer.

sentences.zh: 漢東京曰上林苑令及丞各一人，隸少府。

translations.literal: Eastern Capital Han called it Shanglin Park Director and one assistant director each, subordinate to the Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Capital Han had one Shanglin Park Director and one assistant director, both subordinate to the Privy Treasurer.

sentences.zh: 晉江左闕。

translations.literal: It was absent in Eastern Jin south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: It was not retained in Eastern Jin south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 宋世祖大明三年復置，隸尚書殿中曹及少府。

translations.literal: It was restored in the third year of Daming under Emperor Shizu of Song, subordinate to the Secretariat Palace Affairs bureau and the Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: It was restored in the third year of Daming under Emperor Shizu of Song and placed under both the Secretariat Palace Affairs bureau and the Privy Treasurer.

sentences.zh: 材官將軍，一人。

translations.literal: Material-Works General, one post.
translations.idiomatic: Material-Works General: one post.

sentences.zh: 司馬一人。

translations.literal: One Major.
translations.idiomatic: One Major.

sentences.zh: 主工匠土木之事。

translations.literal: He oversaw craftsmen and earthen construction.
translations.idiomatic: The office oversaw craftsmen and civil construction.

sentences.zh: 漢左右校令，其任也。

translations.literal: The Han Left and Right Workshop Directors held this responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: This had been the responsibility of the Han Left and Right Workshop Directors.

sentences.zh: 魏右校又置材官校尉，主天下材木事。

translations.literal: Under Wei the Right Workshop also established a Material-Works Commandant to oversee timber affairs throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei the Right Workshop also added a Material-Works Commandant to oversee timber affairs empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 晉江左改材官校尉曰材官將軍，又罷左校令。

translations.literal: Eastern Jin south of the Yangtze changed Material-Works Commandant to Material-Works General and abolished the Left Workshop Director.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin south of the Yangtze renamed the Material-Works Commandant Material-Works General and abolished the Left Workshop Director.

sentences.zh: 今材官隸尚書起部及領軍。

translations.literal: At present Material-Works is subordinate to the Secretariat Construction bureau and the Director of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At present Material-Works is subordinate to the Secretariat Construction bureau and the Director of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 侍中，四人。

translations.literal: Palace Attendants, four posts.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendants: four posts.

sentences.zh: 掌奏事，直侍左右，應對獻替。

translations.literal: They presented memorials, served on duty at the sovereign's side, and answered and offered counsel for improvement.
translations.idiomatic: They presented memorials, attended the sovereign on duty, answered questions, and offered counsel for improvement.

sentences.zh: 法駕出，則正直一人負璽陪乘。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriages departed, one Attendant on straight duty carried the seal and rode escort.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriages departed, one Attendant on straight duty carried the seal and rode as escort.

sentences.zh: 殿內門下眾事皆掌之。

translations.literal: All affairs within the palace and under the Inner Gate were under their charge.
translations.idiomatic: All affairs within the palace and under the Inner Gate fell under their charge.

sentences.zh: 周公戒成王立政之篇所云「常伯」，即其任也。

translations.literal: The "Changbo" mentioned in the Duke of Zhou's admonition to King Cheng on establishing governance was this office.
translations.idiomatic: The "Changbo" mentioned in the Duke of Zhou's admonition to King Cheng on establishing governance was this office.

sentences.zh: 侍中本秦丞相史也，使五人往來殿內東廂奏事，故謂之侍中。

translations.literal: Palace Attendants were originally Qin Chancellor clerks; five men were sent back and forth to the eastern wing of the hall to present memorials, hence the name Attendant Within.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendants were originally Qin Chancellor clerks; five men were sent back and forth to the hall's eastern wing to present memorials, hence the name Attendant Within.

sentences.zh: 漢西京無員，多至數十人，入侍禁中，分掌乘輿服物，下至褻器虎子之屬。

translations.literal: Western Capital Han had no fixed quota, often reaching several dozen men; they entered service in the forbidden precinct and divided oversight of imperial carriage accoutrements and garments down to chamber pots and tiger-shaped urinals.
translations.idiomatic: Western Capital Han set no fixed quota, and the number often reached several dozen; they served inside the forbidden precinct and divided oversight of imperial carriage gear and garments down to chamber pots and tiger-shaped urinals.

sentences.zh: 武帝世，孔安國為侍中，以其儒者，特聽掌御唾壺，朝廷榮之。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu's time Kong Anguo served as Palace Attendant; because he was a Confucian scholar, he was specially permitted to hold the imperial spittoon, and the court regarded this as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu, Kong Anguo served as Palace Attendant; because he was a Confucian scholar, he was specially allowed to hold the imperial spittoon—a mark of honor at court.

sentences.zh: 久次者為僕射。

translations.literal: The senior by tenure became Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The senior by tenure became Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 漢東京又屬少府，猶無員。

translations.literal: Eastern Capital Han again subordinated them to the Privy Treasurer, still with no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Capital Han again placed them under the Privy Treasurer, still with no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 掌侍左右，贊導眾事，顧問應答。

translations.literal: They oversaw attendance at the sovereign's side, guided and presented affairs, and consulted and answered.
translations.idiomatic: They attended the sovereign's side, guided and presented affairs, and answered consultations.

sentences.zh: 法駕出，則多識者一人負傳國璽，操斬白蛇劍，參乘；

translations.literal: When the imperial carriages departed, the most knowledgeable one carried the dynastic seal, wielded the Sword that Slew the White Serpent, and rode escort;
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriages departed, the most knowledgeable Attendant carried the dynastic seal, wielded the Sword that Slew the White Serpent, and rode as escort;

sentences.zh: 餘皆騎，在乘輿車後。

translations.literal: the rest all rode horseback behind the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: the rest all rode on horseback behind the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 光武世，改僕射為祭酒焉。

translations.literal: In Guangwu's time the Vice Director was changed to Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangwu the Vice Director was renamed Libationer.

sentences.zh: 漢世，與中官俱止禁中。

translations.literal: In Han times they lodged in the forbidden precinct together with eunuch officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times they lodged inside the forbidden precinct together with eunuch officials.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，侍中莽何羅挾刃謀逆，由是侍中出禁外，有事乃入，事畢即出。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu's time the Attendant Mang Heluo drew a blade in attempted rebellion; thereafter Attendants stayed outside the forbidden precinct, entering only when needed and leaving when finished.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu the Attendant Mang Heluo drew a blade in an attempted rebellion; thereafter Attendants were kept outside the forbidden precinct, entering only when needed and leaving once business was done.

sentences.zh: 王莽秉政，侍中復入，與中官共止。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang held power, Attendants re-entered and lodged together with eunuch officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang held power, Attendants re-entered the forbidden precinct and again lodged with eunuch officials.

sentences.zh: 章帝元和中，侍中郭舉與後宮通，拔佩刀驚御，舉伏誅，侍中由是復出外。

translations.literal: In Yuanhe under Emperor Zhang, Attendant Guo Ju had relations with the harem, drew his sword and alarmed the sovereign; Guo was executed, and Attendants were again moved outside.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe under Emperor Zhang, Attendant Guo Ju had relations with the harem, drew his sword, and alarmed the sovereign; Guo was executed, and Attendants were again moved outside the forbidden precinct.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以來，置四人，別加官不主數。

translations.literal: Since Wei and Jin, four were established; additional appointments did not count toward the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei and Jin four posts were established, and additional appointments did not count toward the quota.

sentences.zh: 秩比二千石。

translations.literal: Rank equivalent to two thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: The rank was equivalent to two thousand shi.
